title.zh: 卷五十一 列傳第一: 后妃上
title.raw: 卷五十一 列傳第一: 后妃上 Volume 51 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts 1

sentences.zh: 三代宮禁之職，《周官》最詳。

translations.literal: The duties of the palace inner quarters through the Three Dynasties are set forth in greatest detail in the Rites of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The offices of the palace inner quarters across the Three Dynasties are described most fully in the Rites of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 自周已降，彤史沿革，各載本書，此不備述。

translations.literal: From the Zhou dynasty onward, the evolution of the red-record offices has been recorded in each respective work; that is not fully recounted here.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhou, changes in the court record-keepers have been documented in their respective histories, which will not be rehearsed here in full.

sentences.zh: 唐因隋制，皇后之下，有貴妃、淑妃、德妃、賢妃各一人，為夫人，正一品；

translations.literal: Tang followed the Sui system; beneath the empress there was one each of Noble Consort, Cultivated Consort, Virtuous Consort, and Worthy Consort, designated as Ladies, of the first rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Tang adopted the Sui framework: below the empress stood four consorts—Noble, Cultivated, Virtuous, and Worthy—each one person, titled Ladies of the first rank;

sentences.zh: 昭儀、昭容、昭媛、修儀、修容、修媛、充儀、充容、充媛各一人，為九嬪，正二品；

translations.literal: one each of Bright Lady, Bright Beauty, Bright Fair One, Cultivated Lady, Cultivated Beauty, Cultivated Fair One, Fulfilling Lady, Fulfilling Beauty, and Fulfilling Fair One, constituting the Nine Concubines, of the second rank;
translations.idiomatic: nine ranks of consorts—Bright, Cultivated, and Fulfilling, each in Lady, Beauty, and Fair One grades, one holder apiece—forming the Nine Concubines at the second rank;

sentences.zh: 婕妤九人，正三品；

translations.literal: nine Talented Fair Ones, of the third rank;
translations.idiomatic: nine Talented Fair Ones at the third rank;

sentences.zh: 美人九人，正四品；

translations.literal: nine Beauties, of the fourth rank;
translations.idiomatic: nine Beauties at the fourth rank;

sentences.zh: 才人九人，正五品；

translations.literal: nine Talented Ladies, of the fifth rank;
translations.idiomatic: nine Talented Ladies at the fifth rank;

sentences.zh: 寶林二十七人，正六品；

translations.literal: twenty-seven Treasured Forests, of the sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: twenty-seven Treasured Forests at the sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 御女二十七人，正七品；

translations.literal: twenty-seven Imperial Maidens, of the seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: twenty-seven Imperial Maidens at the seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 采女二十七人，正八品；

translations.literal: twenty-seven Selected Maidens, of the eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: twenty-seven Selected Maidens at the eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 其餘六尚諸司，分典乘輿服御。

translations.literal: The remaining Six Directorates and their bureaus separately administered the imperial carriage, apparel, and furnishings.
translations.idiomatic: The other Six Directorates and their offices separately managed the imperial carriage, wardrobe, and household supplies.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，官名改易，內職皆更舊號。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, official titles were changed, and all inner-palace offices were given new designations.
translations.idiomatic: In 662, official titles were revised and every inner-palace post was renamed.

sentences.zh: 咸亨二年復舊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianheng the former designations were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 671 the old titles were restored.

sentences.zh: 開元中，玄宗以皇后之下立四妃，法帝嚳也。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era, Emperor Xuanzong established four consorts below the empress, following the model of Emperor Ku.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign, Xuanzong placed four consorts beneath the empress, emulating the precedent of Emperor Ku.

sentences.zh: 而后妃四星，一為正后；

translations.literal: Yet among the four stars of empress and consorts, one is the principal empress;
translations.idiomatic: Yet of the four stars symbolizing empress and consorts, only one is the principal empress;

sentences.zh: 今既立正后，復有四妃，非典法也。

translations.literal: now that a principal empress has been installed, to add four consorts as well is not canonical precedent.
translations.idiomatic: to install a principal empress and then add four consorts as well departed from canonical precedent.

sentences.zh: 乃於皇后之下立惠妃、麗妃、華妃等三位，以代三夫人，為正一品；

translations.literal: Therefore beneath the empress three posts were established—Benevolent Consort, Beautiful Consort, and Splendid Consort—to replace the three Ladies, of the first rank;
translations.idiomatic: He therefore placed three consorts—Benevolent, Beautiful, and Splendid—below the empress in place of the three Ladies, all at the first rank;

sentences.zh: 又置芳儀六人，為正二品；

translations.literal: six Fragrant Companions were also appointed, of the second rank;
translations.idiomatic: six Fragrant Companions were added at the second rank;

sentences.zh: 美人四人，為正三品；

translations.literal: four Beauties, of the third rank;
translations.idiomatic: four Beauties at the third rank;

sentences.zh: 才人七人，為正四品；

translations.literal: seven Talented Ladies, of the fourth rank;
translations.idiomatic: seven Talented Ladies at the fourth rank;

sentences.zh: 尚宮、尚儀、尚服各二人，為正五品；

translations.literal: two each for Director of the Palace, Director of Ceremonies, and Director of Apparel, of the fifth rank;
translations.idiomatic: two holders each for the Directors of Palace, Ceremonies, and Apparel at the fifth rank;

sentences.zh: 自六品至九品，即諸司諸典職員品第而序之，後亦參用前號。

translations.literal: From the sixth through the ninth ranks, the staff of the various bureaus and offices were ordered by rank; later the earlier titles were also used in part.
translations.idiomatic: From the sixth through the ninth ranks, personnel in the various bureaus were ranked accordingly; later reigns also drew on the earlier titles.

sentences.zh: 然而三代之政，莫不以賢妃開國，嬖寵傾邦。

translations.literal: Yet in the governance of the Three Dynasties, none failed to see worthy consorts help found a state and favored minions overturn a realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet across the Three Dynasties, worthy consorts had helped found states even as favored minions had toppled them.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢已還，其流浸盛。

translations.literal: From Qin and Han onward, this current grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: From the Qin and Han onward, the trend only intensified.

sentences.zh: 大至移國，小則臨朝，煥車服以王宗枝，裂土壤而侯肺腑，洎末塗淪敗，赤族夷宗。

translations.literal: At its greatest it shifted the realm; at its least it presided over court; regalia blazed as collateral clans were ennobled, territory was carved up to enfeoff kin by marriage—until, when the end came, whole clans were exterminated and lineages wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: At its height it could move the throne; at its lesser degree it could dominate the court—collateral kin bedecked in princely regalia, in-laws enfeoffed with carved-out domains—until, in the final collapse, entire clans were slaughtered and lineages extinguished.

sentences.zh: 高祖龍飛，宮無正寢，而婦言是用，釁起維城。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, the palace had no proper principal residence, and women's counsel was heeded, so strife arose among the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, the palace lacked a proper principal residence, women's counsel held sway, and strife broke out among the imperial sons.

sentences.zh: 大帝孝和，仁而不武，但恣池臺之賞，寧顧衽席之嫌？

translations.literal: The Great Emperor Xiaohé was benevolent but not martial; he indulged only in rewards of pools and terraces—would he ever heed the suspicions of the bedchamber?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaohé was humane but not forceful, lavishing rewards on pools and terraces while ignoring the dangers lurking in his own bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 武室、韋宗，幾危運祚。

translations.literal: The house of Wu and the clan of Wei nearly endangered the dynasty's fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu clan and the Wei faction nearly cost the dynasty its mandate.

sentences.zh: 東京帝后，歿從夫謚，光烈、和熹之類是也。

translations.literal: Eastern capital empresses and consorts, upon death receiving posthumous titles through their husbands—Guanglie and Hexi are examples.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern capital empresses took posthumous titles through their husbands after death—Guanglie and Hexi are cases in point.

sentences.zh: 高宗自號天皇，武氏自稱天后，而韋庶人生有翌聖之名，肅宗欲后張氏，此不經之甚，皆以凶終。

translations.literal: Gaozong styled himself Heavenly Emperor, the Wu clan called herself Heavenly Empress, the commoner-born Wei bore the name Next Sage while living, and Suzong wished to make Lady Zhang empress—these were extreme breaches of propriety, and all met violent ends.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong styled himself Heavenly Emperor; Wu Zetian called herself Heavenly Empress; the common-born Wei was given the title Next Sage in her lifetime; Suzong wished to elevate Lady Zhang—all gross violations of propriety, and all ended in disaster.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以惠妃之愛，擯斥椒宮，繼以太真，幾喪天下。

translations.literal: Xuanzong, through his love for Benevolent Consort, drove out the pepper-palace empress, then installed Taizhen, and nearly lost the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong, infatuated with Benevolent Consort, cast aside his empress, then elevated Yang Guifei and nearly lost the empire.

sentences.zh: 歷觀前古邦家喪敗之由，多基於子弟召禍。

translations.literal: Surveying antiquity, the causes of a state's ruin often lay in sons and younger brothers inviting calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back through history, the ruin of states often began when imperial sons invited disaster.

sentences.zh: 子弟之亂，必始於宮闈不正。

translations.literal: Discord among sons and younger brothers invariably began with disorder in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Strife among imperial sons invariably began with disorder in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 故息隱鬩墻，秦王謀歸東洛；

translations.literal: Thus when Suiyin quarreled at the wall, the Prince of Qin plotted to return to the eastern capital;
translations.idiomatic: When Suiyin and his brothers clashed at the palace wall, the Prince of Qin plotted to withdraw to Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 馬嵬塗地，太子不敢西行。

translations.literal: at Mawei blood soaked the ground, and the crown prince dared not continue west.
translations.idiomatic: at Mawei blood ran in the streets, and the crown prince dared not follow the emperor west.

sentences.zh: 若中有聖善之慈，胡能若是？

translations.literal: Had there been within a mother of sage-like goodness and compassion, how could things have come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Had the inner palace held a mother of true wisdom and compassion, how could such things have happened?

sentences.zh: 《易》曰「家道正而天下定」，不其然歟！

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says, "When the way of the household is correct, the realm is settled"—is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "When the household is in order, the realm is secure"—and is that not exactly so!

sentences.zh: 自後累朝，長秋虛位，或以旁宗入繼，母屬皆微，徒有冊拜之文，諒乏「關雎」之德。

translations.literal: In later reigns across many dynasties, the Autumn Palace seat stood empty; sometimes a collateral branch succeeded, and the mothers' kin were all insignificant—there were only the documents of investiture, and surely they lacked the virtue of "Guan Ju."
translations.idiomatic: In later reigns the empress's seat often stood vacant; when collateral branches succeeded, the mothers' families were insignificant—there were investiture ceremonies on paper, but little of the virtue praised in "Guan Ju."

sentences.zh: 今錄其存於史冊者，為《后妃傳》云。

translations.literal: Now those preserved in the historical records are compiled in the Biographies of Empresses and Consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Those preserved in the historical record are compiled here as the Biographies of Empresses and Consorts.

sentences.zh: 太穆皇后竇氏

translations.literal: Empress Taimu, née Dou
translations.idiomatic: Empress Taimu of the Dou Clan

sentences.zh: 高祖太穆皇后竇氏，京兆始平人，隋定州總管、神武公毅之女也。

translations.literal: Gaozu's Empress Taimu, née Dou, was a native of Shiping in Jingzhao, daughter of Yi, Sui regional inspector of Dingzhou and Duke of Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's Empress Taimu, née Dou, came from Shiping in Jingzhao. She was the daughter of Dou Yi, Sui regional inspector of Dingzhou and Duke of Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 后母，周武帝姊襄陽長公主。

translations.literal: Her mother was the Elder Princess of Xiangyang, elder sister of Emperor Wu of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was the Elder Princess of Xiangyang, a sister of Emperor Wu of the Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 后生而髮垂過頸，三歲與身齊。

translations.literal: When the empress was born her hair hung below the neck; at three it was level with her body.
translations.idiomatic: At birth her hair already reached below her neck; by age three it was as long as she was tall.

sentences.zh: 周武帝特愛重之，養於宮中。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou cherished her especially and raised her in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou doted on her and raised her within the palace.

sentences.zh: 時武帝納突厥女為后，無寵，后尚幼，竊言於帝曰：「四邊未靜，突厥尚強，願舅抑情撫慰，以蒼生為念。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had taken a Turkic woman as empress without favoring her; the empress was still young and whispered to the emperor, "The four borders are not yet calm and the Turks remain strong. I beg my uncle to restrain his feelings and offer comfort, keeping the common people in mind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had taken a Turkic woman as empress but showed her no favor. Though still young, the future empress whispered to him: "The borders are not yet secure and the Turks remain powerful. I beg you, Uncle, to restrain your feelings and treat her with kindness for the sake of the people.

sentences.zh: 但須突厥之助，則江南、關東不能為患矣。

translations.literal: If only Turkic aid is secured, then the lands south of the Yangtze and east of the Pass cannot become a threat."
translations.idiomatic: With Turkic support secured, the south and the eastern provinces cannot threaten us."

sentences.zh: 」武帝深納之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply accepted this counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took her counsel to heart.

sentences.zh: 毅聞之，謂長公主曰：「此女才貌如此，不可妄以許人，當為求賢夫。

translations.literal: When Yi heard of this he said to the Elder Princess, "This girl's talent and beauty are such that she must not be rashly promised to anyone; a worthy husband should be sought for her.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Yi heard of this, he told the Elder Princess, "With talent and beauty like hers, we must not give her away lightly—we should find a worthy husband."

sentences.zh: 」乃於門屏畫二孔雀，諸公子有求婚者，輒與兩箭射之，潛約中目者許之。

translations.literal: He therefore painted two peacocks on the door screen; whenever a young lord came to seek her hand, he was given two arrows to shoot, with a secret agreement that whoever hit the eyes would win her.
translations.idiomatic: He painted two peacocks on the door screen. Whenever a young nobleman came to propose marriage, he was given two arrows; whoever hit the eyes in secret would win her hand.

sentences.zh: 前後數十輩莫能中，高祖後至，兩發各中一目。

translations.literal: Several dozen in succession could not hit the mark; Gaozu came last, and with two shots each struck one eye.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen suitors missed; when Gaozu came last, his two shots each struck one eye.

sentences.zh: 毅大悅，遂歸於我帝。

translations.literal: Yi was greatly pleased and gave her in marriage to our emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yi was overjoyed and gave her to our emperor in marriage.

sentences.zh: 及周武帝崩，后追思如喪所生。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou died, the empress mourned him as though she had lost her own parent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou died, she mourned him as though she had lost a parent of her own.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，后聞而流涕，自投於床曰：「恨我不為男，以救舅氏之難。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, upon hearing the news the empress wept, threw herself on the bed, and said, "I regret that I am not a man, so that I might rescue my uncle's clan from disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui accepted the abdication, she wept upon hearing the news and threw herself on the bed, crying, "I wish I were a man, so I could save my uncle's house from ruin."

sentences.zh: 」毅與長公主遽掩口曰：「汝勿妄言，滅吾族矣！」

translations.literal: Yi and the Elder Princess hastily covered her mouth and said, "Do not speak rashly—you will destroy our whole clan!"
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yi and the Elder Princess quickly clapped a hand over her mouth: "Do not speak such words—you will destroy our entire clan!"

sentences.zh: 后事元貞太后，以孝聞。

translations.literal: The empress served Empress Dowager Yuanzhen and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: She served Empress Dowager Yuanzhen and was renowned for her filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 太后素有羸疾，時或危篤。

translations.literal: The empress dowager had long suffered from wasting illness and was sometimes in critical condition.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager had long suffered from a wasting illness and was sometimes near death.

sentences.zh: 諸姒以太后性嚴懼譴，皆稱疾而退，惟后晝夜扶侍，不脫衣履者，動淹旬月焉。

translations.literal: The other daughters-in-law, fearing punishment because of the empress dowager's stern nature, all claimed illness and withdrew; only the empress attended day and night without removing her clothes or shoes, often for more than ten days at a stretch.
translations.idiomatic: The other daughters-in-law, fearing the empress dowager's stern temper, all pleaded illness and withdrew. Only she attended day and night without removing her clothes or shoes, often for weeks on end.

sentences.zh: 善書學，類高祖之書，人不能辯。

translations.literal: She was skilled in calligraphy and learning; her hand resembled Gaozu's, and people could not tell them apart.
translations.idiomatic: She was accomplished in calligraphy and scholarship; her handwriting resembled Gaozu's so closely that no one could tell them apart.

sentences.zh: 工篇章，而好存規戒。

translations.literal: She was adept at composition and fond of preserving admonitions and warnings.
translations.idiomatic: She wrote well and liked to offer counsel and warnings.

sentences.zh: 大業中，高祖為扶風太守，有駿馬數匹。

translations.literal: During the Daye era, when Gaozu was regional inspector of Fufeng, he had several fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign, when Gaozu was prefect of Fufeng, he owned several fine horses.

sentences.zh: 常言於高祖曰：「上好鷹愛馬，公之所知，此堪進御，不可久留，人或言者，必為身累，願熟思之。

translations.literal: She often said to Gaozu, "The emperor above loves hawks and prizes horses—as you know, these are fit to present to the court and must not be kept long. If someone speaks of it, it will surely bring trouble upon you; I beg you to think this through carefully.
translations.idiomatic: She often told him, "You know how fond the emperor is of hawks and horses. These are fit to present to court and must not be kept long—if word reaches the wrong ears, you will bring ruin on yourself. Think this through carefully."

sentences.zh: 」高祖未決，竟以此獲譴。

translations.literal: Gaozu could not decide, and in the end was punished on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu hesitated, and in the end was punished for keeping them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，后崩於涿郡，時年四十五。

translations.literal: Before long the empress died in Zhuo Commandery at the age of forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Before long she died in Zhuo Commandery at the age of forty-five.

sentences.zh: 高祖追思后言，方為自安之計，數求鷹犬以進之，俄而擢拜將軍，因流涕謂諸子曰：「我早從汝母之言，居此官久矣。

translations.literal: Gaozu, recalling the empress's words, then devised a plan for his own security, repeatedly seeking hawks and hounds to present upward; soon he was promoted to general. He wept and told his sons, "Had I followed your mother's counsel earlier, I would have held this office long ago.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling her words, Gaozu devised a plan for his own safety, repeatedly presenting hawks and hounds to the court; soon he was promoted to general. Weeping, he told his sons, "Had I heeded your mother sooner, I would have held this rank long ago."

sentences.zh: 」初葬壽安陵，後祔葬獻陵。

translations.literal: She was first buried at Shou'an Mausoleum and later removed for joint burial at Xian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She was first buried at Shou'an Mausoleum and later reinterred beside him at Xian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 上元元年八月，改上尊號曰太穆順聖皇后。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Shangyuan, her honorific title was changed to Empress Taimu Shunsheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of 674, her posthumous honorific was raised to Empress Taimu the Sagely and Accomplished.

sentences.zh: 文德皇后長孫氏

translations.literal: Empress Wende, née Zhangsun
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wende of the Zhangsun Clan

sentences.zh: 太宗文德順聖皇后長孫氏，長安人，隋右驍衛將軍晟之女也。

translations.literal: Taizong's Empress Wende Shunsheng, née Zhangsun, was a native of Chang'an, daughter of Sheng, Sui general of the Right Xiaowei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's Empress Wende the Sagely and Accomplished, née Zhangsun, came from Chang'an. She was the daughter of Zhangsun Sheng, a Sui general of the Right Xiaowei Guard.

sentences.zh: 晟妻，隋揚州刺史高敬德女，生后。

translations.literal: Sheng's wife was the daughter of Gao Jingde, Sui regional inspector of Yangzhou, who bore the empress.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was the daughter of Gao Jingde, Sui regional inspector of Yangzhou, who bore the future empress.

sentences.zh: 少好讀書，造次必循禮則。

translations.literal: From youth she loved reading and in every situation observed ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood she loved books and observed ritual propriety in every situation.

sentences.zh: 年十三，嬪於太宗。

translations.literal: At thirteen she became a consort of Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen she entered Taizong's household as his consort.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，常歸寧於永興里，后舅高士廉媵張氏，於后所宿舍外見大馬，高二丈，鞍勒皆具，以告士廉。

translations.literal: During the Sui Daye era she often returned to her family home in Yongxing Lane; the empress's uncle Gao Shilian's attendant Lady Zhang, outside the lodging where the empress stayed, saw a great horse two zhang in height with saddle and bridle fully equipped, and reported this to Shilian.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui Daye reign she often visited her family home in Yongxing Lane. Her uncle Gao Shilian's attendant Lady Zhang saw outside her quarters a great horse two zhang tall, fully saddled and bridled, and reported it to Shilian.

sentences.zh: 命筮之，遇《坤》之《泰》，筮者曰：「至哉坤元，萬物資生，乃順承天。

translations.literal: He ordered divination performed; the hexagram Kun changing to Tai was obtained, and the diviner said, "How supreme is Kun, source of all things, from which the myriad beings receive life—it follows and receives Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He had divination performed. The result was Kun changing to Tai. The diviner said, "How supreme is Kun, source of all things, from which the myriad beings receive life—it follows and receives Heaven.

sentences.zh: 坤厚載物，德合無疆。

translations.literal: Kun is thick and bears all things; its virtue joins with boundlessness.
translations.idiomatic: Kun is thick and bears all things; its virtue joins with boundlessness.

sentences.zh: 牝馬地類，行地無疆。

translations.literal: The mare belongs to the earth category and traverses the earth without limit.
translations.idiomatic: The mare belongs to the earth and traverses the earth without limit.

sentences.zh: 變而之《泰》，內陽而外陰，內健而外順，是天地交而萬物通也。

translations.literal: Changing to Tai: yang within and yin without, strength within and compliance without—this is Heaven and Earth in communion and the myriad things in communication.
translations.idiomatic: Changing to Tai: yang within and yin without, strength within and compliance without—Heaven and Earth in communion and the myriad things in harmony.

sentences.zh: 《象》曰：后以輔相天地之宜而左右人也。

translations.literal: The Image says: the queen assists in harmonizing Heaven and Earth's appropriateness and thereby guides the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Image says: the queen assists in harmonizing Heaven and Earth and thereby guides the people.

sentences.zh: 龍，《乾》之象也。

translations.literal: The dragon is the image of Qian.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon is the image of Qian.

sentences.zh: 馬，《坤》之象也。

translations.literal: The horse is the image of Kun.
translations.idiomatic: The horse is the image of Kun.

sentences.zh: 變而為《泰》，天地交也。

translations.literal: Changing to Tai means Heaven and Earth in communion.
translations.idiomatic: Changing to Tai means Heaven and Earth in communion.

sentences.zh: 繇協於《歸妹》，婦人之兆也。

translations.literal: The line texts accord with Guimei—a woman's omen.
translations.idiomatic: The line texts accord with Guimei—the omen of a great woman.

sentences.zh: 女處尊位，履中居順也。

translations.literal: A woman occupying the honored position, treading the center and dwelling in compliance.
translations.idiomatic: A woman in the honored position, treading the center and dwelling in compliance.

sentences.zh: 此女貴不可言。

translations.literal: This woman's nobility is beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: This woman's nobility is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 」武德元年，冊為秦王妃。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude she was invested as Princess of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In 618 she was invested as Princess of Qin.

sentences.zh: 時太宗功業既高，隱太子猜忌滋甚。

translations.literal: At that time Taizong's achievements were already great, and the Hidden Crown Prince's suspicion grew ever sharper.
translations.idiomatic: By then Taizong's achievements were already great, and the Hidden Crown Prince's suspicion grew ever sharper.

sentences.zh: 后孝事高祖，恭順妃嬪，盡力彌縫，以存內助。

translations.literal: The empress served Gaozu filially, was respectful and compliant toward the consorts, and strove to mend relations so as to preserve domestic support.
translations.idiomatic: She served Gaozu filially, treated the consorts with respect, and did all she could to mend relations within the household.

sentences.zh: 及難作，太宗在玄武門，方引將士入宮授甲，后親慰勉之，左右莫不感激。

translations.literal: When the crisis broke out, Taizong was at Xuanwu Gate just leading officers into the palace to be given armor; the empress personally comforted and encouraged them, and none present was not moved.
translations.idiomatic: When crisis broke out at Xuanwu Gate, Taizong was leading officers into the palace to arm them. She personally comforted and encouraged the troops, and all present were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 九年，冊拜皇太子妃。

translations.literal: In the ninth year she was invested as consort of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In 626 she was invested as consort of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, she was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong ascended the throne, she was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 贈后父晟司空、齊獻公。

translations.literal: Her father Sheng was posthumously granted Minister of Works and the title Duke of Qixian.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Zhangsun Sheng was posthumously made Minister of Works and Duke of Qixian.

sentences.zh: 后性尤儉約，凡所服御，取給而已。

translations.literal: The empress's nature was especially frugal; whatever she wore or used was only what sufficed.
translations.idiomatic: She was exceptionally frugal, taking only what she needed for dress and daily use.

sentences.zh: 太宗彌加禮待，常與后論及賞罰之事，對曰：「牝雞之晨，惟家之索。

translations.literal: Taizong treated her with ever greater courtesy and often discussed rewards and punishments with her; she replied, "When the hen crows at dawn, the household is undone.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong treated her with ever greater respect and often discussed rewards and punishments with her. She replied, "When the hen crows at dawn, the household is undone.

sentences.zh: 妾以婦人，豈敢豫聞政事？

translations.literal: I am but a woman—how dare I presume to hear of state affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: I am only a woman—how dare I presume to hear of state affairs?"

sentences.zh: 」太宗固與之言，竟不之答。

translations.literal: Taizong pressed the conversation, but in the end she would not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong pressed the point, but she would not answer.

sentences.zh: 時后兄無忌，夙與太宗為布衣之交，又以佐命元勛，委以腹心，出入臥內，將任之朝政。

translations.literal: At that time her elder brother Wuji had long been Taizong's friend from commoner days and, as a founding merit-holder, was entrusted as a confidant, entering and leaving the sleeping quarters; he was about to be placed in charge of court governance.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother Zhangsun Wuji had been Taizong's friend since their commoner days and, as a founding merit-holder, was his closest confidant, with access even to the sleeping quarters. Taizong was about to place him at the head of government.

sentences.zh: 后固言不可，每乘間奏曰：「妾既托身紫宮，尊貴已極，實不願兄弟子侄布列朝廷。

translations.literal: The empress firmly said this must not be done and whenever she found an opening would submit, "Having entrusted myself to the Purple Palace, my honor is already at its height; I truly do not wish my brothers, sons, and nephews arrayed throughout the court.
translations.idiomatic: She firmly objected and whenever she found an opening told him, "Having entered the Purple Palace, my honor is already complete. I truly do not wish my brothers and nephews spread throughout the court.

sentences.zh: 漢之呂、霍可為切骨之誡，特願聖朝勿以妾兄為宰執。

translations.literal: The Lü and Huo of Han can serve as a warning to the bone; I especially beg the sacred court not to make my brother a chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: The Lü and Huo clans of Han are a warning carved into the bone—I beg Your Majesty not to make my brother chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」太宗不聽，竟用無忌為左武候大將軍、吏部尚書、右僕射。

translations.literal: Taizong would not listen and in the end appointed Wuji General of the Left Martial Guard, Minister of Personnel, and Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong would not listen and appointed Wuji General of the Left Martial Guard, Minister of Personnel, and Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 後又密遣無忌苦求遜職，太宗不獲已而許焉，改授開府儀同三司，后意乃懌。

translations.literal: Later she secretly sent Wuji to plead earnestly to yield his office; Taizong, unable to refuse, consented and transferred him to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies; only then was the empress content.
translations.idiomatic: Later she secretly had Wuji plead to resign his post. Taizong, unable to refuse, agreed and made him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the privileges of the Three Excellencies. Only then was she satisfied.

sentences.zh: 有異母兄安業，好酒無賴。

translations.literal: She had a half-brother Anye who was fond of wine and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: She had a half-brother, Anye, who was a drunkard and a wastrel.

sentences.zh: 獻公之薨也，后及無忌並幼，安業斥還舅氏，后殊不以介意，每請太宗厚加恩禮，位至監門將軍。

translations.literal: When Duke Xian died, the empress and Wuji were both young; Anye drove away their maternal kin, but the empress took no offense and repeatedly asked Taizong to bestow generous favor upon him, until he reached the post of Gate Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Xian died, she and Wuji were still children. Anye had driven away their maternal kin, but she bore no grudge and repeatedly asked Taizong to treat him generously, until he rose to Gate Guard General.

sentences.zh: 及預劉德裕逆謀，太宗將殺之，后叩頭流涕為請命曰：「安業之罪，萬死無赦。

translations.literal: When he became involved in Liu Deyu's treasonous plot and Taizong was about to execute him, the empress kowtowed with tears streaming and pleaded for his life, saying, "Anye's crime deserves ten thousand deaths without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: When he became implicated in Liu Deyu's rebellion and Taizong was about to execute him, she kowtowed with tears and pleaded: "Anye's crime deserves death a thousand times over.

sentences.zh: 然不慈於妾，天下知之，今置以極刑，人必謂妾恃寵以復其兄，無乃為聖朝累乎！

translations.literal: Yet he was never kind to me, and all the realm knows it; if he is now subjected to extreme punishment, people will surely say I used favor to avenge my brother—will this not be a burden upon the sacred court!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was never kind to me, and the whole realm knows it. If he is executed now, people will say I used my favor to avenge my brother—would that not bring shame on Your Majesty's court?"

sentences.zh: 」遂得減死。

translations.literal: He was thereby spared death.
translations.idiomatic: He was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 后所生長樂公主，太宗特所鐘愛，及將出降，敕所司資送倍於長公主。

translations.literal: The empress's daughter, Princess Changle, was especially cherished by Taizong; when she was about to marry, he ordered the relevant offices to provide dowry gifts double those given to an imperial princess by birth.
translations.idiomatic: Her daughter Princess Changle was especially dear to Taizong. When she was about to marry, he ordered officials to provide a dowry twice that given to an imperial princess by birth.

sentences.zh: 魏徵諫曰：「昔漢明帝時，將封皇子，帝曰：『朕子安得同於先帝子乎！

translations.literal: Wei Zheng remonstrated, saying, "In the time of Emperor Ming of Han, when he was about to enfeoff his sons, the emperor said, 'How can my sons be treated the same as the former emperor's sons!
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng remonstrated: "When Emperor Ming of Han was about to enfeoff his sons, he said, 'How can my sons be treated the same as the former emperor's sons!

sentences.zh: 』然謂長主者，良以尊於公主也，情雖有差，義無等別。

translations.literal: ' Yet when speaking of an imperial princess by birth, it is precisely because she ranks above a princess by marriage; though affection may differ, in principle there should be no equality.
translations.idiomatic: ' Yet an imperial princess by birth ranks above a princess by marriage. Affection may differ, but propriety does not permit them to be treated as equals.

sentences.zh: 若令公主之禮有過長主，理恐不可，願陛下思之。

translations.literal: If the ceremonial treatment of a princess by marriage exceeds that of an imperial princess by birth, I fear this cannot be justified by reason; I beg Your Majesty to consider this."
translations.idiomatic: If a princess by marriage receives greater honors than an imperial princess by birth, that cannot be justified. I beg Your Majesty to reconsider."

sentences.zh: 」太宗以其言退而告后，后嘆曰：「嘗聞陛下重魏徵，殊未知其故。

translations.literal: Taizong withdrew with these words and told the empress, who sighed and said, "I had heard that Your Majesty valued Wei Zheng, but never knew the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong withdrew and told her. She sighed and said, "I had heard Your Majesty valued Wei Zheng, but never understood why.

sentences.zh: 今聞其諫，實乃能以義制主之情，可謂正直社稷之臣矣。

translations.literal: Now hearing his remonstrance, he truly can restrain the sovereign's feelings through righteousness—he may be called a upright minister of the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear his remonstrance and see that he can restrain the sovereign's feelings through righteousness—he is truly a pillar of the state."

sentences.zh: 妾與陛下結髮為夫婦，曲蒙禮待，情義深重，每言必候顏色，尚不敢輕犯威嚴，況在臣下，情疏禮隔，故韓非為之說難，東方稱其不易，良有以也。

translations.literal: I have been bound to Your Majesty in marriage from the first, graciously treated with ceremony, our bond deep in feeling and duty; with every word I must watch your expression and still dare not lightly transgress your majesty—how much more for subjects below, distant in feeling and separated by ritual! Thus Han Fei wrote on the difficulty of remonstrance, and Dongfang spoke of its hardship; there is good reason for this.
translations.idiomatic: I have been Your Majesty's wife from the beginning, graciously treated, our bond deep in feeling and duty. With every word I watch your expression and still dare not lightly offend you—how much harder for subjects below, distant in feeling and separated by ritual! Han Fei wrote on the difficulty of remonstrance, and Dongfang spoke of its hardship; they knew what they were talking about.

sentences.zh: 忠言逆於耳而利於行，有國有家者急務，納之則俗寧，杜之則政亂，誠願陛下詳之，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Loyal words grate on the ear yet benefit conduct; for those who possess state and family this is an urgent matter. Accept them and custom is settled; block them and governance falls into disorder. I earnestly beg Your Majesty to consider this carefully, and the realm will be greatly blessed.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal words grate on the ear yet benefit conduct. For any ruler this is urgent: accept them and the realm is at peace; block them and governance falls into chaos. I earnestly beg Your Majesty to heed this—the realm will be greatly blessed.

sentences.zh: 」后因請遣中使賫帛五百匹，詣徵宅以賜之。

translations.literal: The empress then asked to send a palace envoy bearing five hundred bolts of silk to Wei's residence as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: She then asked to send a palace envoy with five hundred bolts of silk to Wei's residence as a reward.

sentences.zh: 太子承乾乳母遂安夫人常白后曰：「東宮器用闕少，欲有奏請。

translations.literal: The crown prince Chengan's wet nurse, Lady Sui'an, often told the empress, "The Eastern Palace lacks furnishings and wishes to submit a request.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Chengan's wet nurse, Lady Sui'an, often told her, "The Eastern Palace lacks furnishings and wishes to make a request.

sentences.zh: 」后不聽，曰：「為太子，所患德不立而名不揚，何憂少於器物也！」

translations.literal: The empress would not listen and said, "As crown prince, what one should fear is that virtue is not established and fame not spread abroad—why worry about having too few furnishings!"
translations.idiomatic: She refused and said, "As crown prince, what you should fear is that virtue is not established and fame not won—why worry about having too few furnishings!"

sentences.zh: 八年，從幸九成宮，染疾危惙，太子承乾入侍，密啟后曰：「醫藥備盡，尊體不瘳，請奏赦囚徒，並度人入道，冀蒙福助。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, accompanying the emperor to Jiucheng Palace, she fell gravely ill; Crown Prince Chengan attended her and secretly reported to the empress, "Medicine has been exhausted and Your Majesty's person does not recover; I beg to memorialize for amnesty of prisoners and ordination of people into the Way, hoping to receive blessed aid."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, while accompanying the emperor to Jiucheng Palace, she fell gravely ill. Crown Prince Chengan attended her and secretly reported: "Medicine has failed and Your Majesty does not recover. I beg to memorialize for amnesty of prisoners and ordination of people into the clergy, hoping for divine aid."

sentences.zh: 」后曰：「死生有命，非人力所加。

translations.literal: The empress said, "Life and death have their allotted span and are not within human power to alter.
translations.idiomatic: She said, "Life and death are fated and lie beyond human power.

sentences.zh: 若修福可延，吾素非為惡。

translations.literal: If cultivating merit could extend life, I have never been one to do evil.
translations.idiomatic: If cultivating merit could extend life, I have never been wicked.

sentences.zh: 若行善無效，何福可求？

translations.literal: If doing good is ineffective, what blessing can be sought?
translations.idiomatic: If doing good is ineffective, what blessing can be sought?

sentences.zh: 赦者，國之大事；

translations.literal: Amnesty is a great matter of state;
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty is a great matter of state;

sentences.zh: 佛道者，示存異方之教耳，非惟政體靡弊，又是上所不為，豈以吾一婦人而亂天下法？

translations.literal: Buddhism and Daoism merely show that foreign teachings exist—they not only undermine the body politic but are also what the sovereign above does not practice; how could I, a single woman, overturn the laws of the realm?
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism and Daoism merely show that foreign teachings exist—they undermine governance and are what the sovereign does not practice. How could I, one woman, overturn the laws of the realm?

sentences.zh: 」承乾不敢奏，以告左僕射房玄齡，玄齡以聞，太宗及侍臣莫不噓唏。

translations.literal: Chengan dared not memorialize this and told Left Vice Director Fang Xuanling; Xuanling reported it, and Taizong and the attending officials all sighed with emotion.
translations.idiomatic: Chengan dared not memorialize this and told Left Vice Director Fang Xuanling. Xuanling reported it, and Taizong and all present were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 朝臣咸請肆赦，太宗從之；

translations.literal: The court officials all requested a general amnesty, and Taizong agreed;
translations.idiomatic: Court officials all requested a general amnesty, and Taizong agreed;

sentences.zh: 后聞之，固爭，乃止。

translations.literal: when the empress heard of it she firmly objected, and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: when she heard, she firmly objected, and it was stopped.

sentences.zh: 將大漸，與太宗辭訣，時玄齡以譴歸第，后固言：「玄齡事陛下最久，小心謹慎，奇謀秘計，皆所預聞，竟無一言漏泄，非有大故，願勿棄之。

translations.literal: As her illness became critical, taking leave of Taizong, at that time Xuanling had been reprimanded and returned home; the empress firmly said, "Xuanling has served Your Majesty longest, careful and cautious; strange stratagems and secret plans—all were heard by him, yet not a single word was leaked. Unless there is a great cause, I beg you not to cast him aside.
translations.idiomatic: As her end approached, she took leave of Taizong. Fang Xuanling had been reprimanded and sent home. She firmly said, "Xuanling has served you longest—careful, cautious, privy to every secret plan, yet never a word leaked. Unless there is grave cause, do not cast him aside.

sentences.zh: 又妾之本宗，幸緣姻戚，既非德舉，易履危機，其保全永久，慎勿處之權要，但以外戚奉朝請，則為幸矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, my own clan, fortunate through marriage ties, was not raised by virtue and easily treads on dangerous ground; for their lasting preservation, take care not to place them in positions of power—if they merely attend court as maternal kin, that will be fortune enough.
translations.idiomatic: My own clan rose through marriage, not merit, and easily treads on dangerous ground. For their lasting safety, never place them in positions of power—let them merely attend court as maternal kin, and that will be fortune enough.

sentences.zh: 妾生既無益於時，今死不可厚費。

translations.literal: In life I was of no benefit to the age; in death I must not be expensively buried.
translations.idiomatic: In life I was of no benefit to the age; in death I must not be expensively buried.

sentences.zh: 且葬者，藏也，欲人之不見。

translations.literal: Moreover, burial means concealment—one wishes people not to see.
translations.idiomatic: Burial means concealment—one wishes not to be seen.

sentences.zh: 自古聖賢，皆崇儉薄，惟無道之世，大起山陵，勞費天下，為有識者笑。

translations.literal: From antiquity sages and worthies have all honored frugality; only in ages without the Way have great mountain tombs been raised, exhausting the realm's resources, to the laughter of those with understanding.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity sages have honored frugality; only in lawless ages have great tombs been raised, exhausting the realm, to the laughter of the wise.

sentences.zh: 但請因山而葬，不須起墳，無用棺槨，所須器服，皆以木瓦，儉薄送終，則是不忘妾也。

translations.literal: I only ask to be buried following the mountain contours, without raising a mound, without using coffin or outer case; whatever vessels and garments are needed, let them all be of wood and tile. A frugal funeral will be not forgetting me.
translations.idiomatic: Only bury me along the mountain contours, without raising a mound or using a coffin. Let vessels and garments be of wood and tile. A frugal funeral will be your way of remembering me.

sentences.zh: 」十年六月己卯，崩於立政殿，時年三十六。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the tenth year, on the day jimao, she died in Lizheng Hall at the age of thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of 636, on the day jimao, she died in Lizheng Hall at the age of thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月庚寅，葬於昭陵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year, on the day gengyin, she was buried at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of that year, on the day gengyin, she was buried at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 后嘗撰古婦人善事，勒成十卷，名曰《女則》，自為之序。

translations.literal: The empress once compiled good deeds of ancient women, carved into ten scrolls entitled Standards for Women, and wrote the preface herself.
translations.idiomatic: She once compiled good deeds of ancient women into ten scrolls entitled Standards for Women, writing the preface herself.

sentences.zh: 又著論駁漢明德馬皇后，以為不能抑退外戚，令其當朝貴盛，乃戒其龍馬水車，此乃開其禍源而防其末事耳。

translations.literal: She also wrote a treatise criticizing Empress Ma the Bright and Virtuous of Han, holding that she could not restrain and dismiss maternal kin, allowing them to hold exalted positions at court; she only warned against dragon horses and water carts—this was opening the source of disaster while guarding against its final consequences.
translations.idiomatic: She also wrote a treatise criticizing Empress Ma of Han, arguing that Ma failed to restrain her maternal kin, allowing them to dominate court, and only warned against dragon horses and water carts—opening the source of disaster while guarding against its consequences.

sentences.zh: 且戒主守者曰：「此吾以自防閑耳。

translations.literal: Moreover she warned the custodian, saying, "This is for my own self-restraint.
translations.idiomatic: She warned the custodian: "This is for my own self-restraint.

sentences.zh: 婦人著述無條貫，不欲至尊見之，慎勿言。

translations.literal: A woman's writings lack systematic order; I do not wish the sovereign to see them—take care not to speak of this.
translations.idiomatic: A woman's writings lack systematic order. I do not wish the sovereign to see them—say nothing of this.

sentences.zh: 」崩後，宮司以聞，太宗覽而增慟，以示近臣曰：「皇后此書，足可垂於後代。

translations.literal: After her death the palace offices reported this; Taizong read it and was moved to deeper grief, showing it to close ministers and saying, "The empress's book can truly be handed down to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: After her death the palace reported this. Taizong read it and grieved more deeply, showing it to close ministers: "The empress's book can truly be handed down to posterity.

sentences.zh: 我豈不達天命而不能割情乎！

translations.literal: Do I not understand Heaven's mandate yet cannot sever affection!
translations.idiomatic: Do I not understand Heaven's mandate yet cannot sever my feelings!

sentences.zh: 以其每能規諫，補朕之闕，今不復聞善言，是內失一良佐，以此令人哀耳！

translations.literal: Because she could always offer remonstrance and counsel, supplementing my shortcomings—now I no longer hear good words; within I have lost a fine assistant. For this reason it is heartbreaking!
translations.idiomatic: She could always remonstrate and counsel, supplementing my shortcomings—now I hear no more good words. I have lost a fine counselor within, and that is heartbreaking!

sentences.zh: 」上元元年八月，改上尊號曰文德順聖皇后。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Shangyuan, her honorific title was changed to Empress Wende Shunsheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of 674, her posthumous honorific was raised to Empress Wende the Sagely and Accomplished.

sentences.zh: 賢妃徐氏

translations.literal: Worthy Consort, Lady Xu
translations.idiomatic: Worthy Consort of the Xu Clan

sentences.zh: 太宗賢妃徐氏，名惠，右散騎常侍堅之姑也。

translations.literal: Taizong's Worthy Consort, Lady Xu, named Hui, was the niece of Right Regular Attendant Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's Worthy Consort Xu Hui was the niece of Right Regular Attendant Xu Jian.

sentences.zh: 生五月而能言，四歲誦《論語》、《毛詩》，八歲好屬文。

translations.literal: At five months she could speak; at four she recited the Analects and Mao's Odes; at eight she loved composing literary works.
translations.idiomatic: At five months she could speak; at four she recited the Analects and Mao's Odes; at eight she loved to write.

sentences.zh: 其父孝德試擬《楚辭》，云「山中不可以久留」，詞甚典美。

translations.literal: Her father Xiaode, testing her, had her compose in the style of the Songs of Chu the line "One cannot long remain in the mountains"—the wording was very classical and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Xiaode tested her by asking her to compose in the style of the Songs of Chu the line "One cannot long remain in the mountains"—her wording was elegant and refined.

sentences.zh: 自此遍涉經史，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: From then on she ranged broadly through the classics and histories, never setting down her scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: From then on she ranged through the classics and histories, never setting down her books.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之，納為才人。

translations.literal: When Taizong heard of this, he took her in as a Talented Lady.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong heard of this, he took her into the palace as a Talented Lady.

sentences.zh: 其所屬文，揮翰立成，詞華綺贍。

translations.literal: Whatever she composed with the brush was completed at once, her diction splendid and rich.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever she wrote was completed at once, her prose splendid and rich.

sentences.zh: 俄拜婕妤，再遷充容。

translations.literal: Soon she was appointed Talented Fair One, then promoted again to Fulfilling Fair One.
translations.idiomatic: Soon she was made Talented Fair One, then promoted to Fulfilling Fair One.

sentences.zh: 時軍旅亟動，宮室互興，百姓頗倦勞役，上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: At that time military campaigns were frequent and palaces rose one after another; the common people were quite weary of corvée labor, and she submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Military campaigns were frequent and palaces rose one after another; the people were weary of labor. She submitted a memorial of remonstrance:

sentences.zh: 「自貞觀已來，二十有二載，風調雨順，年登歲稔，人無水旱之弊，國無饑饉之災。

translations.literal: Since the Zhenguan era there have been twenty-two years of favorable winds and timely rain, abundant harvests year after year, the people free from flood and drought harm, the state free from famine disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhenguan era, twenty-two years have passed with favorable weather and abundant harvests, the people free from flood and drought, the state free from famine.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武守文之常主，猶登刻玉之符；

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wu of Han, a ruler who merely maintained established norms, still ascended to perform the jade-inscription rite;
translations.idiomatic: Even Emperor Wu of Han, a ruler who merely maintained established norms, performed the jade-inscription rite;

sentences.zh: 齊桓小國之庸君，尚圖泥金之事。

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Qi, a mediocre lord of a small state, still aspired to the gold-inscription ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: even Duke Huan of Qi, a mediocre lord of a small state, aspired to the gold-inscription ceremony.

sentences.zh: 望陛下推功損己，讓德不居。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will push forward merit and reduce the self, yield virtue and not occupy it.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will attribute merit to others and yield virtue rather than claim it.

sentences.zh: 億兆傾心，猶闕告成之禮；

translations.literal: The hundred million people incline their hearts, yet the Report of Completion rite is still lacking;
translations.idiomatic: The hundred million people look to you with devotion, yet the Report of Completion rite has not been performed;

sentences.zh: 雲亭佇謁，未展升中之儀。

translations.literal: at Yun and Ting they wait in attendance, yet the Mount Tai ascent ceremony has not been carried out.
translations.idiomatic: at Yun and Ting they await your arrival, yet the Mount Tai ascent ceremony has not been performed.

sentences.zh: 此之功德，足以咀嚼百王，網羅千代者矣。

translations.literal: Such merit and virtue are sufficient to digest the hundred kings and encompass a thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Such merit and virtue surpass the hundred kings and encompass a thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 古人有云：「雖休勿休」，良有以也。

translations.literal: The ancients said, "Though at rest, do not rest"—there is good reason for this.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "Though at rest, do not rest"—and they knew what they were talking about.

sentences.zh: 守初保末，聖哲罕兼。

translations.literal: Guarding the beginning and preserving the end—sages and worthies rarely achieve both.
translations.idiomatic: Guarding the beginning and preserving the end—sages rarely achieve both.

sentences.zh: 是知業大者易驕，願陛下難之；

translations.literal: Thus one knows that when achievement is great, arrogance comes easily—I beg Your Majesty to find this difficult;
translations.idiomatic: Great achievement breeds arrogance—I beg Your Majesty to guard against that;

sentences.zh: 善始者難終，願陛下易之。

translations.literal: those who begin well find the end difficult—I beg Your Majesty to find the end easy.
translations.idiomatic: those who begin well find the end hard—I beg Your Majesty to make the end easy.

sentences.zh: 「竊見頃年已來，力役兼總，東有遼海之軍，西有昆丘之役，士馬疲於甲胄，舟車倦於轉輸。

translations.literal: I have observed that in recent years corvée labor has been combined and piled up: in the east there is the Liaohai army, in the west the Kunqiu campaign; soldiers and horses are exhausted in armor, boats and carts wearied in transport.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years corvée labor has piled up: in the east the Liaohai campaign, in the west the Kunqiu expedition. Soldiers and horses are exhausted in armor; boats and carts wearied in transport.

sentences.zh: 且召募役戍，去留懷死生之痛；

translations.literal: Moreover, recruiting men for garrison service, those who depart and those who remain both harbor the pain of life and death;
translations.idiomatic: Recruits for garrison duty, whether departing or remaining, harbor the pain of life and death;

sentences.zh: 因風阻浪，人米有漂溺之危。

translations.literal: blocked by wind and waves, men and grain face the peril of drifting and drowning.
translations.idiomatic: wind and waves block the way, and men and grain face drowning.

sentences.zh: 一夫力耕，卒無數十之獲；

translations.literal: One man labors in the fields yet in the end gains not even a tenth part;
translations.idiomatic: One man labors in the fields yet gains scarcely a tenth of the harvest;

sentences.zh: 一船致損，則傾數百之糧。

translations.literal: one ship lost overturns grain enough for hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: one ship lost spills grain enough to feed hundreds.

sentences.zh: 是猶運有盡之農功，填無窮之巨浪，圖未獲之他眾，喪已成之我軍。

translations.literal: This is like transporting finite agricultural labor to fill endless great waves, plotting to gain an enemy force not yet obtained while losing our army already formed.
translations.idiomatic: This is like pouring finite farm labor into endless waves, seeking an enemy not yet defeated while losing our own army already in the field.

sentences.zh: 雖除凶伐暴，有國常規；

translations.literal: Though punishing the vicious and attacking the violent is the regular practice of a state;
translations.idiomatic: Though punishing the vicious is the regular practice of any state;

sentences.zh: 然黷武玩兵，先哲所戒。

translations.literal: yet taking military affairs lightly and playing with arms is what the sages of old warned against.
translations.idiomatic: taking military affairs lightly is what the sages warned against.

sentences.zh: 昔秦皇並吞六國，反速危亡之基；

translations.literal: Formerly the First Emperor of Qin swallowed the six states, yet swiftly laid the foundation for peril and ruin;
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor of Qin swallowed the six states, yet swiftly laid the foundation for his own ruin;

sentences.zh: 晉武奄有三方，翻成覆敗之業。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin encompassed the three regions, yet turned it into the enterprise of overturn and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin encompassed the realm, yet turned it into the enterprise of his own defeat.

sentences.zh: 豈非矜功恃大，棄德而輕邦；

translations.literal: Was this not because they prized achievement and relied on greatness, abandoned virtue and treated the realm lightly;
translations.idiomatic: Was this not because they prized achievement and relied on greatness, abandoned virtue and treated the realm lightly;

sentences.zh: 圖利忘害，肆情而縱欲？

translations.literal: sought profit and forgot harm, indulged feeling and gave free rein to desire?
translations.idiomatic: sought profit and forgot harm, indulged desire without restraint?

sentences.zh: 遂使悠悠六合，雖廣不救其亡；

translations.literal: Thus the vast six directions, though wide, could not save their ruin;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the vast realm, though wide, could not save them from ruin;

sentences.zh: 嗷嗷黎庶，因弊以成其禍。

translations.literal: the crying common people, through exhaustion, brought their calamity to completion.
translations.idiomatic: the common people, through exhaustion, brought calamity upon themselves.

sentences.zh: 是知地廣非常安之術，人勞乃易亂之源。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that vast territory is not the method of lasting peace, and human exhaustion is the source of easy disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Vast territory is not the path to lasting peace; exhausted people are the source of disorder.

sentences.zh: 願陛下布澤流人，矜弊恤乏，減行役之煩，增湛露之惠。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to spread bounty and extend kindness to the people, pity the exhausted and relieve the destitute, reduce the burdens of corvée travel, and increase the beneficence of heavy dew.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to spread bounty and kindness, pity the exhausted and relieve the destitute, reduce corvée burdens, and increase your gracious care.

sentences.zh: 妾又聞為政之本，貴在無為。

translations.literal: I have also heard that the root of governance lies in valuing non-action.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that the root of governance lies in non-action.

sentences.zh: 竊見土木之功，不可兼遂。

translations.literal: I observe that earth-and-wood projects cannot all be completed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Construction projects cannot all be completed at once.

sentences.zh: 此闕初建，南營翠微，曾未逾時，玉華創制。

translations.literal: This palace was just built, the southern camp at Cuwei was laid out, and before much time had passed, Yuhua was newly constructed.
translations.idiomatic: This palace was just built, the southern camp at Cuwei laid out, and before much time had passed, Yuhua was newly constructed.

sentences.zh: 雖復因山藉水，非無架築之勞；

translations.literal: Though again following mountains and borrowing waters, there is still no lack of labor in framing and building;
translations.idiomatic: Though built along mountains and waters, there is still no lack of framing and construction;

sentences.zh: 損之又損，頗有工力之費。

translations.literal: reduced again and again, there is still considerable expenditure of labor.
translations.idiomatic: even when reduced again and again, labor costs remain considerable.

sentences.zh: 終以茅茨示約，猶興木石之疲；

translations.literal: in the end using thatched roofs to show restraint, still raises the exhaustion of wood and stone;
translations.idiomatic: Even thatched roofs to show restraint still exhaust wood and stone;

sentences.zh: 假使和雇取人，不無煩擾之弊。

translations.literal: even if hiring laborers with payment, there is no lack of the harm of harassment.
translations.idiomatic: even hiring paid labor brings harassment.

sentences.zh: 是以卑宮菲食，聖主之所安；

translations.literal: Therefore humble palaces and meager food are what sage rulers rest in;
translations.idiomatic: Humble palaces and meager food are what sage rulers rest in;

sentences.zh: 金屋瑤臺，驕主之為麗。

translations.literal: golden chambers and jasper terraces are what arrogant rulers make splendid.
translations.idiomatic: golden chambers and jasper terraces are what arrogant rulers make splendid.

sentences.zh: 故有道之君，以逸逸人；

translations.literal: Thus rulers who possess the Way let the people rest in ease;
translations.idiomatic: Rulers who possess the Way let the people rest;

sentences.zh: 無道之君，以樂樂身。

translations.literal: rulers without the Way take pleasure in their own pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: rulers without the Way take pleasure only in themselves.

sentences.zh: 願陛下使之以時，則力無竭矣；

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to employ labor at the proper seasons, and strength will not be exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: Employ labor at the proper seasons, and strength will not be exhausted;

sentences.zh: 用而息之，則人斯悅矣。

translations.literal: use it and then let it rest, and the people will be pleased.
translations.idiomatic: use it and then let it rest, and the people will be pleased.

sentences.zh: 「夫珍玩伎巧，乃喪國之斧斤；

translations.literal: Precious curios and clever crafts are the axe and adze that destroy a state;
translations.idiomatic: Precious curios and clever crafts are the axe that destroys a state;

sentences.zh: 珠玉錦繡，實迷心之鴆毒。

translations.literal: pearls, jade, brocade, and embroidery are truly the poison that bewilders the heart.
translations.idiomatic: pearls, jade, brocade, and embroidery are poison that bewilders the heart.

sentences.zh: 竊見服玩纖靡，如變化於自然；

translations.literal: I observe that garments and playthings are refined to fineness, as if transformed by nature itself;
translations.idiomatic: Garments and playthings are refined to fineness, as if transformed by nature itself;

sentences.zh: 織貢珍奇，若神仙之所制。

translations.literal: woven tribute and rare objects seem made by immortals.
translations.idiomatic: woven tribute and rare objects seem made by immortals.

sentences.zh: 雖馳華於季俗，實敗素於淳風。

translations.literal: Though they race with splendor in the fashion of the age, they truly destroy simplicity in the pure custom.
translations.idiomatic: Though they dazzle in the fashion of the age, they destroy the simplicity of pure custom.

sentences.zh: 是知漆器非延叛之方，桀造之而人叛；

translations.literal: Thus one knows lacquer vessels are not the method of prolonging loyalty—Jie made them and people rebelled;
translations.idiomatic: Lacquer vessels do not prolong loyalty—Jie made them and people rebelled;

sentences.zh: 玉杯豈招亡之術，紂用之而國亡。

translations.literal: jade cups are hardly the art of inviting ruin—Zhou used them and the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: jade cups hardly invite ruin—Zhou used them and the state perished.

sentences.zh: 方驗侈麗之源，不可不遏。

translations.literal: One has just verified the source of extravagance and splendor—it cannot go unchecked.
translations.idiomatic: The source of extravagance has been verified—it cannot go unchecked.

sentences.zh: 作法於儉，猶恐其奢；

translations.literal: Establish law in frugality and one still fears extravagance;
translations.idiomatic: Establish law in frugality and one still fears extravagance;

sentences.zh: 作法於奢，何以制後？

translations.literal: establish law in extravagance—how can one restrain those who come after?
translations.idiomatic: establish law in extravagance—how can one restrain posterity?

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下明鑒未形，智周無際，窮奧秘於麟閣，盡探賾於儒林。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's clear perception reaches what is not yet formed, wisdom encompasses without limit, exhausts mysteries in the Unicorn Pavilion, and fully probes the profound in the forest of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's clear perception reaches what is not yet formed, your wisdom without limit—you exhaust mysteries in the Unicorn Pavilion and probe the profound in the forest of scholars.

sentences.zh: 千王治亂之蹤，百代安危之跡，興衰禍福之數，得失成敗之機，故亦苞吞心府之中，循環目圍之內，乃宸衷之久察，無假一二言焉。

translations.literal: The tracks of a thousand kings in ordering and disordering, the traces of a hundred generations in safety and peril, the reckoning of rise and decline, fortune and calamity, the keys to gain and loss, success and failure — all these are likewise enclosed within the heart's inner chamber and revolve within the scope of the eyes. They are matters the imperial heart has long scrutinized, and for which a word or two is needless.
translations.idiomatic: How a thousand kings brought order or chaos, how safety and peril passed through a hundred generations, the calculus of rise and fall, fortune and disaster, gain and loss, victory and defeat — all of this already lies folded within Your Majesty's heart and passes before Your eyes. You have long pondered such things; a few words from me can add nothing.

sentences.zh: 惟恐知之非難，行之不易，志驕於業泰，體逸於時安。

translations.literal: I only fear that knowing is not difficult but doing is not easy, that the will grows proud when the enterprise flourishes, and the body grows lax when the times are peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: My fear is simply this: to know is easy, but to act is hard; when the realm thrives, ambition turns to pride; when the age is at peace, discipline gives way to ease.

sentences.zh: 伏願抑志裁心，慎終如始，削輕過以添重德，循今是以替前非，則令名與日月無窮，盛業與乾坤永大。」

translations.literal: I humbly wish that you restrain ambition and trim the heart, treat the end as carefully as the beginning, pare away light faults to add weighty virtue, and follow present rightness to replace past wrongs — then your fine name will be endless as sun and moon, and your great enterprise eternally vast as heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty will curb ambition and discipline the heart, guard the end as you guarded the beginning, shed small faults to add weight to your virtue, and let present right conduct replace past error — then your good name will endure with the sun and moon, and your great enterprise stand forever with heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 太宗善其言，優賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong approved her words and rewarded her generously.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong praised what she had said and bestowed rich favors upon her.

sentences.zh: 及太宗崩，追思顧遇之恩，哀慕愈甚，發疾不自醫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong died, she recalled the kindness he had shown her; her grief and longing grew ever deeper. She fell ill and would not treat herself.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's death, she brooded on the grace he had shown her; grief and longing overwhelmed her. She fell ill and refused medical care.

sentences.zh: 病甚，謂所親曰：「吾荷顧實深，志在早歿，魂其有靈，得侍園寢，吾之志也。

translations.literal: When her illness was severe, she said to those close to her: "I owe him so deep a kindness that my wish is to die soon. If my soul has any power, to attend his tomb-garden is my desire."
translations.idiomatic: As the illness worsened, she told her intimates, "I owe him so much that I wish only to die soon. If my spirit has any power, my desire is to serve at his tomb."

sentences.zh: 」因為七言詩及連珠以見其志。

translations.literal: Thereupon she composed heptasyllabic verse and linked pearls to express her intent.
translations.idiomatic: She then wrote heptasyllabic poems and linked-pearl verses to declare her resolve.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年卒，時年二十四，詔贈賢妃，陪葬於昭陵之石室。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui she died, aged twenty-four. An edict posthumously granted her the title Worthy Consort, and she was buried with honor in a stone chamber at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the first year of Yonghui, at the age of twenty-four. The court posthumously enfeoffed her as Worthy Consort and buried her in a stone chamber at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 廢后王氏

translations.literal: Deposed Empress Wang
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Empress Wang

sentences.zh: 高宗廢后王氏，并州祁人也。

translations.literal: Empress Wang, whom Emperor Gaozong deposed, was a native of Qi in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang, whom Emperor Gaozong deposed, came from Qi in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父仁祐，貞觀中羅山令。

translations.literal: Her father Renyou was magistrate of Luoshan during the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Renyou had served as magistrate of Luoshan under Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 同安長公主，即后之從祖母也。

translations.literal: Princess Tong'an the Chang was the empress's grand-aunt on her father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Tong'an the Elder was the empress's grand-aunt.

sentences.zh: 公主以后有美色，言於太宗，遂納為晉王妃。

translations.literal: Because the princess saw that the future empress had great beauty, she spoke of her to Emperor Taizong, and Wang was taken in as consort to the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the girl's great beauty, the princess recommended her to Emperor Taizong, and she was taken into the Jin princely household as consort.

sentences.zh: 高宗登儲，冊為皇太子妃，以父仁祐為陳州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was established as heir apparent, Wang was enfeoffed as crown princess, and her father Renyou was made prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong was named heir, she was installed as crown princess, and her father Renyou was appointed prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，立為皇后，以仁祐為特進、魏國公，母柳氏為魏國夫人。

translations.literal: Early in Yonghui she was installed as empress; Renyou was made Special Advancement and Duke of Wei, and her mother, Lady Liu, was made Lady of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yonghui she was made empress; Renyou was granted Special Advancement and the title Duke of Wei, and her mother, Lady Liu, was enfeoffed as Lady of Wei.

sentences.zh: 仁祐尋卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: Renyou soon died and was posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Renyou died soon afterward and was posthumously honored as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 初，武皇后貞觀末隨太宗嬪御居於感業寺，后及左右數為之言，高宗由是復召入宮，立為昭儀。

translations.literal: At first, in the late Zhenguan period, Empress Wu, as one of Taizong's consorts, lived at Ganye Temple. The empress and her attendants repeatedly spoke well of her, and for this reason Gaozong summoned her back to the palace and made her zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the late Zhenguan years, Wu — later empress — had lived at Ganye Temple as one of Taizong's consorts. The empress and her attendants repeatedly praised her, and Gaozong therefore recalled her to the palace and made her Concubine of Bright Deportment.

sentences.zh: 俄而漸承恩寵，遂與后及良娣蕭氏遞相譖毀。

translations.literal: Before long she gradually received imperial favor, and then she, the empress, and Lady Xiao the liangdi took turns slandering one another.
translations.idiomatic: Before long she won the emperor's favor, and she, the empress, and Lady Xiao the liangdi began to slander one another in turn.

sentences.zh: 帝終不納后言，而昭儀寵遇日厚。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end did not accept the empress's words, while the zhaoyi's favor daily grew deeper.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed the empress, and the zhaoyi's favor grew day by day.

sentences.zh: 后懼不自安，密與母柳氏求巫祝厭勝。

translations.literal: The empress, fearing and ill at ease, secretly with her mother Lady Liu sought shamans and witchcraft for suppressive victory rites.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful and unsettled, the empress secretly joined her mother Lady Liu in seeking shamans and curse-magic.

sentences.zh: 事發，帝大怒，斷柳氏不許入宮中，后舅中書令柳奭罷知政事，並將廢后，長孫無忌、褚遂良等固諫，乃止。

translations.literal: When the matter came out, the emperor was furious, cut off Lady Liu from entering the palace, dismissed the empress's maternal uncle, Chancellor Liu Shi, from directing state affairs, and was about to depose the empress; Zhangsun Wuji, Chu Suiliang, and others firmly remonstrated, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was exposed, the emperor flew into a rage, forbade Lady Liu the palace, and removed the empress's uncle, Chancellor Liu Shi, from office. He was on the point of deposing the empress when Zhangsun Wuji, Chu Suiliang, and others remonstrated forcefully, and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 俄又納李義府之策，永徽六年十月，廢后及蕭良娣皆為庶人，囚之別院。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he adopted Li Yifu's plan; in the tenth month of the sixth year of Yonghui, both the empress and Lady Xiao the liangdi were made commoners and imprisoned in a separate courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he accepted Li Yifu's counsel. In the tenth month of the sixth year of Yonghui, the empress and Lady Xiao the liangdi were both reduced to commoners and confined in a separate courtyard.

sentences.zh: 武昭儀令人皆縊殺之。

translations.literal: Wu the zhaoyi had people strangle them all to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wu the zhaoyi had them all strangled.

sentences.zh: 后母柳氏、兄尚衣奉御全信及蕭氏兄弟，並配流嶺外。

translations.literal: The empress's mother Lady Liu, her brother the Director of Palace Attendants Quanxin, and the Xiao brothers were all sentenced to exile beyond the Ling Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's mother Lady Liu, her brother Quanxin of the Palace Attendants Office, and the Xiao brothers were all banished beyond the Ling Mountains.

sentences.zh: 遂立昭儀為皇后。

translations.literal: The zhaoyi was then installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The zhaoyi was then made empress.

sentences.zh: 尋又追改后姓為蟒氏，蕭良娣為梟氏。

translations.literal: Soon afterward their surnames were retroactively changed: the empress to Mang, Lady Xiao to Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward their surnames were retroactively changed — the empress to Mang, "Python," and Lady Xiao to Xiao, "Owl."

sentences.zh: 良娣蕭氏

translations.literal: Lady Xiao the liangdi
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xiao the liangdi

sentences.zh: 庶人良娣初囚，大罵曰：「願阿武為老鼠，吾作貓兒，生生扼其喉！

translations.literal: When the commoner lady was first imprisoned, she cursed loudly: "May Wu become a rat and I become a cat — life after life I shall throttle her throat!"
translations.idiomatic: When the commoner lady was first imprisoned, she cursed loudly: "May that Wu become a rat and I a cat — life after life I shall choke her throat!"

sentences.zh: 」武后怒，自是宮中不畜貓。

translations.literal: Empress Wu was furious; from then on cats were not kept in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was enraged, and from that time forward no cats were kept in the palace.

sentences.zh: 初囚，高宗念之，閑行至其所，見其室封閉極密，惟開一竅通食器出入。

translations.literal: When they were first imprisoned, Gaozong thought of them and, walking at leisure, came to their place. He saw the rooms sealed extremely tight, with only a small opening for food vessels to pass in and out.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after their imprisonment, Gaozong thought of them and strolled to their quarters. He found the rooms sealed tight, with only a small hole through which food vessels could pass.

sentences.zh: 高宗惻然，呼曰：「皇后、淑妃安在？

translations.literal: Gaozong was moved with pity and called out: "Where are the empress and the Pure Consort?"
translations.idiomatic: Moved to pity, Gaozong called out, "Where are the empress and the Pure Consort?"

sentences.zh: 」庶人泣而對曰：「妾等得罪，廢棄為宮婢，何得更有尊稱，名為皇后？

translations.literal: The commoner wept and answered: "We have offended and been cast aside as palace maids — how can we still have honored titles and be called empress?"
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, the commoner replied, "We have sinned and been cast out as palace maids — how can we still bear honored titles and be called empress?"

sentences.zh: 」言訖悲咽，又曰：「今至尊思及疇昔，使妾等再見日月，出入院中，望改此院名為『回心院』，妾等再生之幸。

translations.literal: When she had spoken, she sobbed, and added: "Now Your Majesty thinks of former days and has let us see sun and moon again, going in and out within the courtyard. We beg that this courtyard be renamed 'Courtyard of Returning Hearts' — that would be the fortune of our rebirth."
translations.idiomatic: She broke off in sobs, then said, "Now that Your Majesty remembers old days and has let us see daylight again, moving freely within this courtyard, we beg that it be renamed the Courtyard of Returning Hearts — that would be our rebirth."

sentences.zh: 」高宗曰：「朕即有處置。

translations.literal: Gaozong said: "I shall immediately make arrangements."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong said, "I shall see to it at once."

sentences.zh: 」武后知之，令人杖庶人及蕭氏各一百，截去手足，投於酒甕中，曰：「令此二嫗骨醉！

translations.literal: When Empress Wu learned of it, she had the commoner and Lady Xiao each beaten one hundred strokes with clubs, their hands and feet cut off, and cast into wine jars, saying: "Let these two hags get drunk to the bone!"
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu learned of this, she had the commoner and Lady Xiao each flogged one hundred strokes, their hands and feet cut off, and thrown into wine jars, saying, "Let these two crones get drunk to the bone!"

sentences.zh: 」數日而卒。

translations.literal: Within several days they died.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days they were dead.

sentences.zh: 後則天頻見王、蕭二庶人披發瀝血，如死時狀。

translations.literal: Later Wu Zetian frequently saw the two commoners Wang and Xiao with disheveled hair dripping blood, just as at their deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wu Zetian repeatedly saw the two commoners Wang and Xiao, hair loose and blood streaming, exactly as they had been at death.

sentences.zh: 武后惡之，禱以巫祝，又移居蓬萊宮，復見，故多在東都。

translations.literal: Empress Wu detested this, prayed through shamans, and moved to Penglai Palace; she still saw them, and therefore often stayed in the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu loathed the visions, sought relief through shamans, and moved to Penglai Palace, but still saw them — and so she spent much of her time in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，復后姓為王氏，梟氏還為蕭氏。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, the empress's surname was restored to Wang, and the Owl surname was returned to Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong ascended the throne, the empress's surname was restored to Wang and the Owl surname was changed back to Xiao.

sentences.zh: 和思皇后趙氏

translations.literal: Empress Zhao, the Harmonious-Reflecting Empress
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhao, the Harmonious-Reflecting Empress

sentences.zh: 韋庶人

translations.literal: Commoner Lady Wei
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei, the Deposed Consort

sentences.zh: 帝在房州時，常謂后曰：「一朝見天日，誓不相禁忌。

translations.literal: When the emperor was in Fangzhou, he often said to the empress: "Once I see the light of day again, I swear we shall impose no mutual restrictions."
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was in exile at Fangzhou, he often told the empress, "When I see daylight again, I swear we shall place no restrictions on each other."

sentences.zh: 」及得志，受上官昭容邪說，引武三思入宮中，升御床，與后雙陸，帝為點籌，以為歡笑，醜聲日聞於外。

translations.literal: When he got his wish, accepting the wicked counsel of Shangguan Zhaorong, he brought Wu Sansi into the palace, had him ascend the imperial couch, play backgammon with the empress while the emperor kept score — all for amusement. The ugly rumors daily reached outside.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had his wish, he listened to the corrupt advice of Shangguan Zhaorong, brought Wu Sansi into the palace, and had him climb onto the imperial bed to play backgammon with the empress while the emperor kept score for their amusement. Scandalous reports spread day by day beyond the palace.

sentences.zh: 乃大出宮女，雖左右內職，亦許時出禁中。

translations.literal: He then released large numbers of palace women; even inner attendants were allowed to leave the forbidden precincts at times.
translations.idiomatic: He then released large numbers of palace women, and even inner attendants were permitted to leave the forbidden precincts from time to time.

sentences.zh: 上官氏及宮人貴幸者，皆立外宅，出入不節，朝官邪佞者候之，恣為狎遊，祈其賞秩，以至要官。

translations.literal: Shangguan and favored palace women all established outer residences, coming and going without restraint. Flattering officials waited on them, indulging in familiar recreation, seeking rewards and ranks, even reaching high office.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan and favored palace women all set up houses outside the palace and came and went without restraint. Sycophantic court officials waited on them, indulging in intimate revelry and seeking rewards and promotion — some even reaching the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 時侍中敬暉謀去諸武，武三思患之，乃結上官氏以為援，因得幸於后，潛入宮中謀議，乃諷百官上帝尊號為應天皇帝，后為順天皇后。

translations.literal: At that time Vice-Director Jing Hui plotted to remove the Wus; Wu Sansi was alarmed and allied with Shangguan as support, thereby gaining the empress's favor.
