He secretly entered the palace for consultations and induced the hundred officials to petition that the emperor take the honorific title Responding-to-Heaven Emperor and the empress Following-Heaven Empress.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Vice-Director Jing Hui plotted to purge the Wu faction. Alarmed, Wu Sansi allied with Shangguan as his patron, won the empress's favor, and entered the palace in secret to plot. He then prompted the officials to petition that the emperor take the title Responding-to-Heaven Emperor and the empress Following-Heaven Empress.

sentences.zh: 帝與后親謁太廟，告謝受尊號之意。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress personally visited the Imperial Ancestral Temple to announce and give thanks for receiving the honorific titles.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress personally visited the Imperial Ancestral Temple to announce and give thanks for the new honorific titles.

sentences.zh: 於是三思驕橫用事，敬暉、王同皎相次夷滅，天下咸歸咎於后。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sansi became arrogant and ran affairs; Jing Hui and Wang Tongjiao were destroyed in succession, and all under heaven blamed the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Sansi grew arrogant and wielded power. Jing Hui and Wang Tongjiao were destroyed one after another, and all under heaven laid the blame on the empress.

sentences.zh: 后方優寵親屬，內外封拜，遍列清要。

translations.literal: The empress then lavishly favored her kin; within and without they were enfeoffed and promoted, filling every exalted post.
translations.idiomatic: The empress then showered favor on her kin, enfeoffing and promoting them within and without until they filled every exalted post.

sentences.zh: 又欲寵樹安樂公主，乃制公主開府，置官屬。

translations.literal: Wishing also to elevate and establish Princess Anle, she decreed that princesses might open offices and appoint staff.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking also to elevate Princess Anle, she decreed that princesses might establish offices and appoint staffs.

sentences.zh: 太平公主儀比親王。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping's ceremonial array matched that of an imperial prince.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping's ceremonial honors matched those of an imperial prince.

sentences.zh: 長寧、安樂二府不置長史而已。

translations.literal: The Changning and Anle establishments lacked only a chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The Changning and Anle establishments differed from a princely household only in lacking a chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 宜城公主等以非后所生，各減太平之半。

translations.literal: Princesses such as Yicheng, who were not born of the empress, each had half of Taiping's allotment.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses such as Yicheng, who were not the empress's own daughters, each received half of Taiping's honors.

sentences.zh: 安樂恃寵驕恣，賣官鬻獄，勢傾朝廷，常自草制敕，掩其文而請帝書焉，帝笑而從之，竟不省視。

translations.literal: Anle, relying on favor, was arrogant and unrestrained; she sold offices and peddled judgments, her power overturning the court. She often drafted edicts herself, covered the text, and asked the emperor to sign — he laughed and agreed, never even examining them.
translations.idiomatic: Anle, secure in favor, grew arrogant and unrestrained. She sold offices and judgments until her power overshadowed the court. She often drafted edicts herself, covered the text, and asked the emperor to sign them. He laughed and complied, never even reading them.

sentences.zh: 又請自立為皇太女，帝雖不從，亦不加譴。

translations.literal: She also asked to be made heir apparent in her own right as Grand Crown Princess; the emperor did not agree, but neither did he rebuke her.
translations.idiomatic: She also asked to be made heir in her own right as Grand Crown Princess. The emperor refused, but did not rebuke her.

sentences.zh: 所署府僚，皆猥濫非才。

translations.literal: The staff she appointed to her office were all unworthy and without talent.
translations.idiomatic: The officials she appointed to her household were all unworthy men without real ability.

sentences.zh: 又廣營第宅，侈靡過甚。

translations.literal: She also built mansions on a vast scale, with extravagance beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: She also built mansions on a vast scale, with extravagance beyond all bounds.

sentences.zh: 長寧及諸公主叠相仿效，天下咸嗟怨之。

translations.literal: Changning and the other princesses piled imitation upon imitation; all under heaven sighed and resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Changning and the other princesses followed suit one after another, and all under heaven sighed and resented them.

sentences.zh: 神龍三年，節湣太子死後，宗楚客率百僚上表，加后號為順天翊聖皇后。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shenlong, after the Crown Prince of Jiemin died, Zong Chuke led the hundred officials in a memorial adding to the empress the title Shunsheng Empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shenlong, after the death of Crown Prince Jiemin, Zong Chuke led the hundred officials in a memorial adding to the empress the title Following-Heaven Assisting-Sage Empress.

sentences.zh: 景龍二年春，宮中希旨，妄稱后衣箱中有五色雲出，帝使畫工圖之，出示於朝，乃大赦天下，百僚母妻各加邑號。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Jinglong, sycophants in the palace falsely claimed five-colored clouds issued from the empress's clothing chest. The emperor had painters depict it and display it at court, then granted a great amnesty, and each official's mother and wife received an added fief title.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Jinglong, palace sycophants falsely claimed that five-colored clouds had issued from the empress's clothing chest. The emperor had painters depict the marvel and display it at court, then proclaimed a great amnesty and granted added fief titles to every official's mother and wife.

sentences.zh: 右驍衛將軍、知太史事迦葉誌忠上表曰：

translations.literal: General of the Right Xiaowei Guards, Overseer of the Directorate of Astronomy, Ye Zhizhong submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: General of the Right Xiaowei Guards and overseer of the Directorate of Astronomy, Ye Zhizhong, submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 「昔高祖未受命時，天下歌《桃李子》；

translations.literal: "In former times, before Gaozu received the Mandate, all under heaven sang 'Peach and Plum';
translations.idiomatic: "In former times, before Emperor Gaozu received the Mandate, the realm sang Peach and Plum;

sentences.zh: 太宗未受命時，天下歌《秦王破陣樂》；

translations.literal: before Taizong received the Mandate, all under heaven sang 'Prince of Qin Breaks the Battle Array';
translations.idiomatic: before Taizong received the Mandate, the realm sang The Prince of Qin's Battle Array;

sentences.zh: 高宗未受命時，天下歌《側堂堂》；

translations.literal: before Gaozong received the Mandate, all under heaven sang 'Leaning Tall and Grand';
translations.idiomatic: before Gaozong received the Mandate, the realm sang Leaning Tall and Grand;

sentences.zh: 天后未受命時，天下歌《武媚娘》。

translations.literal: before the Empress of Heaven received the Mandate, all under heaven sang 'Lady Wu Meiniang.'
translations.idiomatic: before the Empress of Heaven received the Mandate, the realm sang Lady Wu Meiniang.

sentences.zh: 伏惟應天皇帝未受命時，天下歌《英王石州》；

translations.literal: I humbly consider that before the Responding-to-Heaven Emperor received the Mandate, all under heaven sang 'Prince of Ying's Shizhou';
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that before the Responding-to-Heaven Emperor received the Mandate, the realm sang The Prince of Ying's Shizhou;

sentences.zh: 順天皇后未受命時，天下歌《桑條韋也》。

translations.literal: before the Following-Heaven Empress received the Mandate, all under heaven sang 'Mulberry Branch and Wei.'
translations.idiomatic: before the Following-Heaven Empress received the Mandate, the realm sang Mulberry Branch and Wei.

sentences.zh: 女行六合之內，齊首蹀足，應四時八節之會，歌舞同歡。

translations.literal: Women throughout the six directions within the realm, heads aligned and feet treading in step, respond to the gatherings of the four seasons and eight festivals, singing and dancing in shared joy.
translations.idiomatic: Women throughout the realm move in step, heads bowed and feet dancing, answering the gatherings of the four seasons and eight festivals in shared song and joy.

sentences.zh: 豈與夫《簫韶》九成、百獸率舞同年而語哉！

translations.literal: How can this be spoken of in the same breath as the nine movements of Shaoyao, when the hundred beasts lead the dance!
translations.idiomatic: Surely this belongs in the same breath as the nine movements of Shaoyao, when the hundred beasts led the dance!

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇后降帝女之精，合為國母，主蠶桑以安天下，后妃之德，於斯為盛。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that the empress descended with the essence of an emperor's daughter, united as mother of the state, presiding over sericulture to settle all under heaven — in the virtue of empress and consort, nothing surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that the empress, born of an emperor's daughter, has become mother of the realm, presiding over sericulture to settle the world — in the virtue of empress and consort, nothing surpasses this.

sentences.zh: 謹進《桑條歌》十二篇，伏請宣布中外，進入樂府，皇后先蠶之時，以享宗廟。」

translations.literal: I respectfully submit twelve sections of the 'Mulberry Branch Song,' humbly requesting that it be proclaimed within and without, entered into the Music Office, and performed when the empress leads the first sericulture rites, to be offered in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully submit twelve sections of the Mulberry Branch Song and humbly ask that it be proclaimed throughout the realm, entered into the Music Office, and performed when the empress leads the first sericulture rites, to be offered before the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 帝悅而許之，特賜誌忠莊一區、雜彩七百段。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and assented, specially granting Zhizhong one estate and seven hundred assorted bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and agreed, specially granting Zhizhong one estate and seven hundred bolts of assorted silks.

sentences.zh: 太常少卿鄭愔又引而申之，播於舞詠，亦受厚賞。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Sacrificial Worships Zheng Yin further expanded on it, spreading it in dance and song, and also received rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Court of Sacrificial Worships Zheng Yin further elaborated on it, spreading it in dance and song, and also received rich rewards.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書宗楚客又諷補闕趙延禧表陳符命，解《桑條》以為十八代之符，請頒示天下，編諸史冊。

translations.literal: Minister of War Zong Chuke additionally prompted Reminder Zhao Yanxi to memorialize on portents, interpreting 'Sangtiao' as a token of eighteen generations, requesting it be proclaimed throughout the realm and entered in the historical record.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Zong Chuke further prompted Reminder Zhao Yanxi to memorialize on portents, interpreting Mulberry Branch as a token of eighteen generations and asking that it be proclaimed throughout the realm and entered in the historical record.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，擢延禧為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and promoted Yanxi to Remonstrating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and promoted Yanxi to Remonstrating Censor.

sentences.zh: 時上官昭容與其母鄭氏及尚宮柴氏、賀婁氏，樹用親黨，廣納貨賂，別降墨敕，斜封授官，或出臧獲屠販之類，累居榮秩。

translations.literal: At that time Shangguan Zhaorong, with her mother Lady Zheng and the Chief of Palace Attendants Chai and Helou, promoted their kin and faction, widely accepted bribes, issued supplementary edicts with slanting seals for appointment — sometimes even slaves, butchers, and peddlers rose to honored ranks in succession.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shangguan Zhaorong, together with her mother Lady Zheng and the Chief of Palace Attendants Chai and Helou, promoted their kin and faction, accepted bribes on a wide scale, and issued supplementary edicts with slanting seals to sell offices — so that slaves, butchers, and peddlers rose in succession to honored rank.

sentences.zh: 又引女巫趙氏出入禁中，封為隴西夫人，勢與上官氏為比。

translations.literal: She also brought in a witch surnamed Zhao to enter and leave the forbidden precincts, enfeoffing her as Lady of Longxi; her power matched Shangguan's.
translations.idiomatic: She also brought a witch surnamed Zhao in and out of the forbidden precincts, enfeoffing her as Lady of Longxi, whose power rivaled Shangguan's own.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，帝將親祠南郊，國子祭酒祝欽明、司業郭山惲建議云：「皇后亦合助祭。

translations.literal: In winter of the third year, when the emperor was about to perform southern suburban sacrifice in person, Director of the Imperial Academy Zhu Qinming and Vice Director Guo Shanyin proposed: "The empress should also assist in the sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year, as the emperor was about to perform the southern suburban sacrifice in person, Director of the Imperial Academy Zhu Qinming and Vice Director Guo Shanyin proposed, "The empress should also assist in the sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 」太常博士唐紹、蔣欽緒上疏爭之。

translations.literal: Academician-Readers Tang Shao and Jiang Qinxu submitted remonstrances disputing this.
translations.idiomatic: Academician-Readers Tang Shao and Jiang Qinxu submitted memorials disputing the proposal.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射韋巨源詳定儀注，遂希旨協同欽明之議。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Wei Juyuan detailed the ritual regulations and, seeking to please, agreed with Qinming's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Wei Juyuan, charged with fixing the ritual regulations, sought to please the throne and sided with Qinming's proposal.

sentences.zh: 帝納其言，以后為亞獻，仍以宰相女為齊娘，以執籩豆。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted their advice; the empress served as second offerer, and a chancellor's daughter served as qiniang bearing baskets and vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted their advice. The empress served as second offerer, and a chancellor's daughter served as attendant maiden bearing the ritual baskets and vessels.

sentences.zh: 欽明又欲請安樂公主為終獻，迫於時議而止。

translations.literal: Qinming also wished to request Princess Anle as final offerer, but stopped under pressure of contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Qinming also wished to request Princess Anle as final offerer, but desisted under pressure of public opinion.

sentences.zh: 四年正月望夜，帝與后微行市裏，以觀燒燈。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth night of the first month of the fourth year, the emperor and empress went incognito into the markets to watch the lantern display.
translations.idiomatic: On the full-moon night of the first month of the fourth year, the emperor and empress went incognito into the city markets to watch the lantern festival.

sentences.zh: 又放宮女數千，夜遊縱觀，因與外人陰通，逃逸不還。

translations.literal: He also released several thousand palace women for night outings to roam and look about; some secretly had relations with outsiders and fled, never returning.
translations.idiomatic: He also released several thousand palace women to roam at night and look about freely. Some secretly took lovers among outsiders and fled, never to return.

sentences.zh: 時國子祭酒葉靜能善符禁小術，散騎常侍馬秦客頗閑醫藥，光祿少卿楊均以調膳侍奉，皆出入宮掖。

translations.literal: At that time Director Ye Jingneng was skilled in talismanic prohibitions and minor arts; Regular Attendant Ma Qinke was well versed in medicine; Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Yang Jun was trusted to prepare food — all entered and left the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Director Ye Jingneng was skilled in talismanic arts and minor magic; Regular Attendant Ma Qinke was well versed in medicine; and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Yang Jun was trusted to prepare food — all of them moved in and out of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 均與秦客皆得幸於后，相次丁母憂，旬日悉起復舊職。

translations.literal: Both Jun and Qinke gained the empress's favor; when they successively completed mourning for their mothers, within ten days all were recalled to their former posts.
translations.idiomatic: Both Yang Jun and Ma Qinke won the empress's favor. When they successively entered mourning for their mothers, all were recalled to their former posts within ten days.

sentences.zh: 時安樂公主與駙馬武延秀、侍中紀處訥、中書令宗楚客、司農卿趙履溫互相猜貳，叠為朋黨。

translations.literal: At that time Princess Anle, her consort Wu Yanxiu, Vice Director Ji Chunna, Grand Secretary Zong Chuke, and Director of the Court of Imperial Granaries Zhao Lüwen distrusted one another in turn and formed rival factions.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Princess Anle, her consort Wu Yanxiu, Vice Director Ji Chunna, Grand Secretary Zong Chuke, and Director of the Court of Imperial Granaries Zhao Lüwen distrusted one another in turn and formed rival factions.

sentences.zh: 六月，帝遇毒暴崩。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the emperor met poison and died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, the emperor was poisoned and died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 時馬秦客侍疾，議者歸罪於秦客及安樂公主。

translations.literal: At the time Ma Qinke was attending his illness; opinion blamed Qinke and Princess Anle.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qinke was attending him at the time, and public opinion blamed Qinke and Princess Anle.

sentences.zh: 后懼，秘不發喪，引所親入禁中，謀自安之策。

translations.literal: The empress was afraid, kept the death secret, summoned her intimates into the forbidden precinct, and plotted measures for her own security.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was afraid. She kept the death secret, summoned her intimates into the forbidden precinct, and plotted how to secure herself.

sentences.zh: 以刑部尚書裴談、工部尚書張錫知政事，留守東都；

translations.literal: She made Minister of Justice Pei Tan and Minister of Works Zhang Xi directors of state affairs, remaining to guard the eastern capital;
translations.idiomatic: She appointed Minister of Justice Pei Tan and Minister of Works Zhang Xi to direct state affairs and remain to guard the eastern capital;

sentences.zh: 又命左金吾大將軍趙承恩及宦者左監門衛大將軍薛崇簡帥兵五百人往筠州，以備譙王重福。

translations.literal: she also ordered General of the Left Jinwu Guard Zhao Chengen and the eunuch Left Supervisor of the Gates Guard Xue Chongjian to lead five hundred troops to Yunzhou to guard against Prince of Qiao Chongfu.
translations.idiomatic: she also ordered General of the Left Jinwu Guard Zhao Chengen and the eunuch Left Supervisor of the Gates Guard Xue Chongjian to lead five hundred troops to Yunzhou to guard against Prince of Qiao Chongfu.

sentences.zh: 后與兄太子少保溫定策，立溫王重茂為皇太子，召諸府兵五萬人屯京城，分為左右營，然後發喪。

translations.literal: The empress with her brother, Crown Prince's Junior Tutor Wen, settled policy: install Prince Wen Chongmao as crown prince, summon fifty thousand garrison troops to camp at the capital divided into left and right camps, and only then announce the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The empress and her brother, Crown Prince's Junior Tutor Wei Wen, settled on a plan: install Prince Wen Chongmao as crown prince, summon fifty thousand garrison troops to camp at the capital in left and right divisions, and only then announce the funeral.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，尊后為皇太后，臨朝攝政。

translations.literal: The young emperor took the throne; the empress was honored as empress dowager and held court to exercise regency.
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor ascended the throne. The empress was honored as empress dowager and held court as regent.

sentences.zh: 韋溫總知內外兵馬，守援宮掖；

translations.literal: Wei Wen held overall command of inner and outer military forces and guarded the palace;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wen held overall command of inner and outer military forces and guarded the palace;

sentences.zh: 駙馬韋捷、韋濯分掌左右屯營；

translations.literal: Consorts Wei Jie and Wei Zhuo separately commanded the left and right encampments;
translations.idiomatic: Consorts Wei Jie and Wei Zhuo separately commanded the left and right encampments;

sentences.zh: 武延秀及溫從子播、族弟璿、外甥高崇，共典左右羽林軍及飛騎、萬騎。

translations.literal: Wu Yanxiu and Wen's nephew Bo, clansman Xuan, and maternal nephew Chong together commanded the Left and Right Feathered Forest Armies, Flying Cavalry, and Ten Thousand Riders.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yanxiu, Wen's nephew Bo, clansman Xuan, and maternal nephew Gao Chong together commanded the Left and Right Feathered Forest Armies, Flying Cavalry, and Ten Thousand Riders.

sentences.zh: 播、璿欲先樹威嚴，拜官日先鞭萬騎數人，眾皆怨，不為之用。

translations.literal: Bo and Xuan wished first to establish stern authority; on the day they received office they first whipped several men of the Ten Thousand Riders. All resented it and would not serve them.
translations.idiomatic: Bo and Xuan sought first to establish their authority. On the day they took office they flogged several men of the Ten Thousand Riders. The men resented it and refused to obey them.

sentences.zh: 時京城恐懼，相傳將有革命之事，往往偶語，人情不安。

translations.literal: At that time the capital was gripped by fear; rumors spread that there would be a dynastic revolution; people often whispered in pairs; hearts were unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the capital was gripped by fear. Rumors spread of an impending dynastic upheaval; people whispered in pairs, and public morale was unsettled.

sentences.zh: 臨淄王率薛崇簡、鐘紹京、劉幽求領萬騎及總監，丁未，入自玄武門，至左羽林軍，斬將軍韋璿、韋播及中郎將高崇於寢帳。

translations.literal: The Prince of Linzi led Xue Chongjian, Zhong Shaojing, and Liu Youqiu at the head of the Ten Thousand Riders and grand directors. On the day dingwei they entered through the Xuanwu Gate, reached the Left Feathered Forest Army, and in the sleeping tent cut down Generals Wei Xuan, Wei Bo, and Captain Gao Chong.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Linzi led Xue Chongjian, Zhong Shaojing, and Liu Youqiu at the head of the Ten Thousand Riders and grand directors. On the day dingwei they entered through the Xuanwu Gate, reached the Left Feathered Forest Army, and in the sleeping tent cut down Generals Wei Xuan and Wei Bo and Captain Gao Chong.

sentences.zh: 遂斬關而入，至太極殿。

translations.literal: They then cut down the gate and entered, reaching the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: They then broke through the gate and entered, reaching the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 后惶駭遁入殿前飛騎營，及武延秀、安樂公主皆為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: The empress, terrified, fled into the Flying Cavalry camp before the hall; Wu Yanxiu and Princess Anle were all killed by the mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: The empress, terrified, fled into the Flying Cavalry camp before the hall. Wu Yanxiu and Princess Anle were all slain by the mutinous troops.

sentences.zh: 分遣萬騎誅其黨與韋溫、溫從子捷，及族弟嬰；

translations.literal: They dispatched the Ten Thousand Riders in separate parties to execute her partisans Wei Wen, Wen's nephew Jie, and clansman Ying;
translations.idiomatic: They dispatched the Ten Thousand Riders in separate parties to execute her partisans Wei Wen, Wen's nephew Jie, and clansman Ying;

sentences.zh: 宗楚客、弟晉卿，紀處訥，馬秦客，葉靜能，楊均，趙履溫，衛尉卿王哲，太常卿李【王曳】，將作少匠李守質及韋氏武氏宗族，無少長皆斬之。

translations.literal: Zong Chuke and his younger brother Jinqing, Ji Chunna, Ma Qinke, Ye Jingneng, Yang Jun, Zhao Lüwen, Director of the Court of Imperial Insignia Wang Zhe, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Li 【Wang Ye】, Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Construction Li Shouzhi, and the Wei and Wu clans — without regard to age, all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke and his younger brother Jinqing, Ji Chunna, Ma Qinke, Ye Jingneng, Yang Jun, Zhao Lüwen, Director of the Court of Imperial Insignia Wang Zhe, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Li 【Wang Ye】, Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Construction Li Shouzhi, and the Wei and Wu clans — young and old alike were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 梟后及安樂公主首於東市。

translations.literal: The empress's and Princess Anle's heads were displayed at the Eastern Market.
translations.idiomatic: The heads of the empress and Princess Anle were displayed at the Eastern Market.

sentences.zh: 翌日，敕收后屍，葬以一品之禮，追貶為庶人；

translations.literal: The next day an edict ordered the empress's corpse collected and buried with first-rank rites, posthumously demoted to commoner status;
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict ordered the empress's body recovered and buried with first-rank rites, while posthumously demoting her to commoner status;

sentences.zh: 安樂公主葬以三品之禮，追貶為悖逆庶人。

translations.literal: Princess Anle was buried with third-rank rites and posthumously demoted to Treacherous Commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anle was buried with third-rank rites and posthumously demoted to Treacherous Commoner.

sentences.zh: 上官昭容

translations.literal: Shangguan Zhaorong
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Zhaorong

sentences.zh: 中宗上官昭容，名婉兒，西臺侍郎儀之孫也。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong's Shangguan Zhaorong, named Wan'er, was the granddaughter of Vice Director of the Western Terrace Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Zhaorong of Emperor Zhongzong, whose personal name was Wan'er, was the granddaughter of Vice Director of the Western Terrace Yi.

sentences.zh: 父庭芝，與儀同被誅，婉兒時在繈褓，隨母配入掖庭。

translations.literal: Her father Tingzhi was executed together with Yi; Wan'er was then in swaddling clothes and, following her mother, was assigned to the Palace Women Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Tingzhi was executed together with Yi. Wan'er was still an infant and, following her mother, was assigned to the Palace Women Quarters.

sentences.zh: 及長，有文詞，明習吏事。

translations.literal: When she grew up, she had literary talent and was well versed in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When she came of age, she possessed literary talent and was well versed in administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 則天時，婉兒忤旨當誅，則天惜其才不殺，但黥其面而已。

translations.literal: During Wu Zetian's reign, Wan'er offended the throne and was due for execution; Wu Zetian prized her talent and did not kill her, but only tattooed her face.
translations.idiomatic: During Wu Zetian's reign, Wan'er offended the throne and was due for execution. Wu Zetian prized her talent and spared her life, tattooing her face instead.

sentences.zh: 自聖歷已後，百司表奏，多令參決。

translations.literal: From the Shenli era onward, memorials from the hundred offices were often submitted to her for joint decision.
translations.idiomatic: From the Shenli era onward, memorials from the hundred offices were often submitted to her for review and decision.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，又令專掌制命，深被信任。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong ascended the throne, she was again put in sole charge of edicts and deeply trusted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong ascended the throne, she was again placed in sole charge of drafting edicts and enjoyed his deep trust.

sentences.zh: 尋拜為昭容，封其母鄭氏為沛國夫人。

translations.literal: Soon she was appointed Zhaorong, and her mother Lady Zheng was enfeoffed as Lady of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Soon she was appointed Zhaorong, and her mother Lady Zheng was enfeoffed as Lady of Pei.

sentences.zh: 婉兒既與武三思淫亂，每下制敕，多因事推尊武后而排抑皇家。

translations.literal: Wan'er had already entered a licentious affair with Wu Sansi; whenever she issued edicts, she often used the occasion to exalt Empress Wu and suppress the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wan'er had already entered a licentious affair with Wu Sansi. Whenever she issued edicts, she often used the occasion to exalt Empress Wu and suppress the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 節湣太子深惡之，及舉兵，至肅章門，扣閣索婉兒。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Jiemin deeply hated her; when he raised troops and reached Su Zhang Gate, he knocked on the gate and demanded Wan'er.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Jiemin deeply hated her. When he raised troops and reached Su Zhang Gate, he knocked on the gate and demanded Wan'er be handed over.

sentences.zh: 婉兒大言曰：「觀其此意，即當次索皇后以及大家。

translations.literal: Wan'er spoke loudly, saying: "Judging by this intent, next he will demand the empress and the Great One.
translations.idiomatic: Wan'er cried out, saying, "Judging by his intent, next he will demand the empress and the Great One.

sentences.zh: 」帝與后遂激怒，並將婉兒登玄武門樓以避兵鋒，俄而事定。

translations.literal: " The emperor and empress were thus enraged; both took Wan'er up onto the Xuanwu Gate tower to avoid the edge of battle, and soon the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor and empress were thus enraged. Both took Wan'er up onto the Xuanwu Gate tower to escape the fighting, and soon the affair was settled.

sentences.zh: 婉兒常勸廣置昭文學士，盛引當朝詞學之臣，數賜遊宴，賦詩唱和。

translations.literal: Wan'er often urged broad appointment of Zhaowen academicians, lavishly inviting the dynasty's literary officials, repeatedly bestowing banquets and tours, composing and exchanging poems.
translations.idiomatic: Wan'er often urged the broad appointment of Zhaowen academicians and lavishly gathered the dynasty's literary officials. She repeatedly granted them banquets and outings, composing and exchanging poems with them.

sentences.zh: 婉兒每代帝及后、長寧安樂二公主，數首並作，辭甚綺麗，時人咸諷誦之。

translations.literal: Wan'er often composed several pieces at once on behalf of the emperor, empress, and the Princesses of Changning and Anle; the language was very ornate, and people of the time all recited them.
translations.idiomatic: Wan'er often composed several pieces at once on behalf of the emperor, empress, and the Princesses of Changning and Anle. The language was richly ornate, and people of the time all recited her verses.

sentences.zh: 婉兒又通於吏部侍郎崔湜，引知政事。

translations.literal: Wan'er also had an affair with Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Cui Shi and had him brought into state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wan'er also had an affair with Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Cui Shi and had him brought into the conduct of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 湜嘗充使開商山新路，功未半而中宗崩，婉兒草遺制，曲敘其功而加褒賞。

translations.literal: Shi had once served as envoy to open a new route through Mount Shang; the work was not yet half done when Emperor Zhongzong died. Wan'er drafted the death edict, bending the narrative to recount his merit and add praise and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Shi had once served as envoy to open a new route through Mount Shang. The work was not yet half done when Emperor Zhongzong died. Wan'er drafted the death edict, bending the narrative to recount his merit and add praise and reward.

sentences.zh: 及韋庶人敗，婉兒亦斬於旗下。

translations.literal: When the Commoner of Wei fell, Wan'er was also beheaded beneath the banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Commoner of Wei fell, Wan'er was also beheaded beneath the army banner.

sentences.zh: 玄宗令收其詩筆，撰成文集二十卷，令張說為之序。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong ordered her poems and writings collected and compiled into a collected works in twenty scrolls, and had Zhang Yue write the preface.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong ordered her poems and writings collected and compiled into a twenty-scroll collected works, and had Zhang Yue write the preface.

sentences.zh: 初，婉兒在孕時，其母夢人遺己大秤，占者曰：「當生貴子，而秉國權衡。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wan'er was in the womb, her mother dreamed that someone gave her a great scale. The diviner said: "She will bear a noble child who will hold the nation's scales of power.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wan'er was in the womb, her mother dreamed that someone gave her a great scale. The diviner said, "You will bear a noble child who will hold the nation's scales of power.

sentences.zh: 」既生女，聞者嗤其無效，及婉兒專秉內政，果如占者之言。

translations.literal: " When a girl was born, those who heard laughed that it had failed; when Wan'er came to hold sole sway over inner governance, it indeed matched the diviner's words.
translations.idiomatic: " When a girl was born, those who heard laughed that the prophecy had failed. Yet when Wan'er came to hold sole sway over inner governance, it proved exactly as the diviner had said.

sentences.zh: 肅明皇后劉氏

translations.literal: Empress Suming, Lady Liu
translations.idiomatic: Empress Suming, Lady Liu

sentences.zh: 睿宗肅明順聖皇后劉氏，刑部尚書德威之孫也。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong's Suming Shunsheng Empress, Lady Liu, was the granddaughter of Minister of Justice Dewei.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong's Suming Shunsheng Empress, Lady Liu, was the granddaughter of Minister of Justice Dewei.

sentences.zh: 父延景，陜州刺史，景雲元年，追贈尚書右僕射、沛國公。

translations.literal: Her father Yanjing was Prefect of Shaan Prefecture; in the first year of Jingyun he was posthumously granted Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Duke of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Yanjing had served as Prefect of Shaan Prefecture. In the first year of Jingyun he was posthumously granted Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Duke of Pei.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，睿宗居籓，納后為孺人，尋立為妃，生寧王憲、壽昌代國二公主。

translations.literal: During Yifeng, Ruizong held a princely fief and took her as Lady; soon she was established as consort and bore Prince of Ning Xian and the Princesses of Shouchang and Daiguo.
translations.idiomatic: During Yifeng, while Ruizong held a princely fief, he took her as Lady and soon established her as consort. She bore Prince of Ning Xian and the Princesses of Shouchang and Daiguo.

sentences.zh: 文明元年睿宗即位，冊為皇后；

translations.literal: In the first year of Wende, when Ruizong ascended the throne, she was invested as empress;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wende, when Ruizong ascended the throne, she was invested as empress;

sentences.zh: 及降為皇嗣，后從降為妃。

translations.literal: When he was reduced to heir apparent, the empress was correspondingly reduced to consort.
translations.idiomatic: When he was reduced to heir apparent, the empress was correspondingly reduced to consort.

sentences.zh: 長壽中，與昭成皇后同被譴，為則天所殺。

translations.literal: During Changshou, she and Empress Zhaocheng were both condemned and killed by Wu Zetian.
translations.idiomatic: During Changshou, she and Empress Zhaocheng were both condemned and killed by Wu Zetian.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，追謚肅明皇后，招魂葬於東都城南，陵曰惠陵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun she was posthumously titled Empress Suming and given a soul-summoning burial south of the Eastern Capital; the mausoleum was called Huiling.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingyun she was posthumously titled Empress Suming and given a soul-summoning burial south of the Eastern Capital. Her mausoleum was called Huiling.

sentences.zh: 睿宗崩，遷祔橋陵。

translations.literal: When Ruizong died, her tablet was moved to be enshrined at Qiaoling.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong died, her tablet was moved to be enshrined at Qiaoling.

sentences.zh: 以昭成太后故，不得入太廟配饗，常別祀於儀坤廟。

translations.literal: Because of Empress Dowager Zhaocheng, she could not enter the Grand Ancestral Temple for joint sacrifice and was regularly worshipped separately at Yikun Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Empress Dowager Zhaocheng, she could not enter the Grand Ancestral Temple for joint sacrifice and was regularly worshipped separately at Yikun Temple.

sentences.zh: 開元二十年，始祔太廟。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Kaiyuan she was first enshrined in the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Kaiyuan she was first enshrined in the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 昭成皇后竇氏

translations.literal: Empress Zhaocheng, Lady Dou
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaocheng, Lady Dou

sentences.zh: 睿宗昭成順聖皇后竇氏，將作大匠抗曾孫也。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong's Zhaocheng Shunsheng Empress, Lady Dou, was the great-granddaughter of the Director of Palace Construction Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong's Zhaocheng Shunsheng Empress, Lady Dou, was the great-granddaughter of the Director of Palace Construction Kang.

sentences.zh: 祖誕，大理卿、莘國公。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Dan was Director of the Court of Judicial Review and Duke of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Dan was Director of the Court of Judicial Review and Duke of Shen.

sentences.zh: 父孝諶，潤州刺史，景雲元年，追贈太尉、邠國公。

translations.literal: Her father Xiaochen was Prefect of Run Prefecture; in the first year of Jingyun he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and Duke of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Xiaochen had served as Prefect of Run Prefecture. In the first year of Jingyun he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and Duke of Bin.

sentences.zh: 后姿容婉順，動循禮則，睿宗為相王時為孺人，甚見禮異。

translations.literal: The empress's bearing was graceful and compliant; in movement she followed ritual norms. When Ruizong was Prince of Xiang she was his Lady and was treated with exceptional honor.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's bearing was graceful and compliant, and in all her conduct she followed ritual propriety. When Ruizong was Prince of Xiang she was his Lady and was treated with exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 光宅元年，立為德妃。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangzhai she was established as Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangzhai she was established as Virtuous Consort.

sentences.zh: 生玄宗及金仙、玉真二公主。

translations.literal: She bore Emperor Xuanzong and the Princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Emperor Xuanzong and the Princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年，為戶婢團兒誣譖與肅明皇后厭蠱咒詛。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changshou, the household maid Tuan'er falsely accused her and Empress Suming of sorcery and curses.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changshou, the household maid Tuan'er falsely accused her and Empress Suming of sorcery and curses.

sentences.zh: 正月二日，朝則天皇后於嘉豫殿，既退而同時遇害。

translations.literal: On the second day of the first month they attended upon Empress Wu Zetian at Jiayu Hall; after withdrawing they were both killed at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the first month they attended upon Empress Wu Zetian at Jiayu Hall. After withdrawing they were both killed at the same time.

sentences.zh: 梓宮秘密，莫知所在。

translations.literal: The imperial coffin was kept secret; no one knew where it lay.
translations.idiomatic: The disposition of the imperial coffin was kept secret, and no one knew where she lay.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，謚曰昭成皇后，招魂葬於都城之南，陵曰靖陵。

translations.literal: When Ruizong ascended the throne, she was posthumously titled Empress Zhaocheng and given a soul-summoning burial south of the capital; the mausoleum was called Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong ascended the throne, she was posthumously titled Empress Zhaocheng and given a soul-summoning burial south of the capital. Her mausoleum was called Jingling.

sentences.zh: 又立廟於京師，號為儀坤廟。

translations.literal: A temple was also established in the capital, named Yikun Temple.
translations.idiomatic: A temple was also established in the capital, named Yikun Temple.

sentences.zh: 睿宗崩，后以帝母之重，追尊為皇太后，謚仍舊，祔葬橋陵，遷神主於太廟。

translations.literal: When Ruizong died, because of her weight as the emperor's mother she was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager with her posthumous title unchanged, buried jointly at Qiaoling, and her spirit tablet moved to the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong died, because of her status as the emperor's mother she was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager with her posthumous title unchanged, buried jointly at Qiaoling, and her spirit tablet moved to the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 廢后王氏

translations.literal: Deposed Empress Wang
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Empress Wang

sentences.zh: 玄宗廢后王氏，同州下邽人，梁冀州刺史神念之後。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong's deposed Empress Wang was a native of Xiagui in Tong Prefecture and a descendant of Shennian, Governor of Ji Prefecture under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong's deposed Empress Wang was a native of Xiagui in Tong Prefecture and a descendant of Shennian, Governor of Ji Prefecture under Liang.

sentences.zh: 上為臨淄王時，納后為妃。

translations.literal: When the emperor was Prince of Linzi, he took her as consort.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was Prince of Linzi, he took her as consort.

sentences.zh: 上將起事，頗預密謀，贊成大業。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to raise the affair, she took part in the secret plotting and helped bring the great enterprise to success.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to launch his coup, she took part in the secret plotting and helped bring the great enterprise to success.

sentences.zh: 先天元年，為皇后，以父仁皎為太僕卿，累加開府儀同三司、邠國公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiantian she became empress; her father Renjiao was made Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and cumulatively promoted to Grand Master with Extraordinary Honors of the First Rank and Duke of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiantian she became empress. Her father Renjiao was made Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and cumulatively promoted to Grand Master with Extraordinary Honors of the First Rank and Duke of Bin.

sentences.zh: 后兄守一以后無子，常懼有廢立，導以符厭之事。

translations.literal: The empress's elder brother Shouyi, because the empress had no son, constantly feared deposition and replacement and led her into talismanic sorcery.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's elder brother Shouyi, fearing that her childlessness would lead to deposition, constantly led her into talismanic sorcery.

sentences.zh: 有左道僧明悟為祭南北斗，刻霹靂木，書天地字及上諱，合而佩之，且祝曰：「佩此有子，當與則天皇后為比。

translations.literal: There was a heterodox monk, Mingwu, who performed sacrifices to the Northern and Southern Dippers, carved thunderbolt wood, wrote the characters for Heaven and Earth and the emperor's taboo name, joined them together for her to wear, and prayed, saying: "Wearing this will bring a son; she shall be the equal of Empress Zetian.
translations.idiomatic: A heterodox monk named Mingwu performed sacrifices to the Northern and Southern Dippers, carved thunderbolt wood, inscribed the characters for Heaven and Earth and the emperor's taboo name, joined them together for her to wear, and prayed, saying, "Wearing this will bring a son; she shall be the equal of Empress Zetian.

sentences.zh: 」事發，上親究之，皆驗。

translations.literal: " When the affair came to light, the emperor personally investigated it, and all was verified.
translations.idiomatic: " When the affair came to light, the emperor personally investigated it, and all was verified.

sentences.zh: 開元十二年秋七月己卯，下制曰：「皇后王氏，天命不祐，華而不實。

translations.literal: On the day jimao of the seventh month of autumn in the twelfth year of Kaiyuan, an edict was issued, saying: "Empress Wang — Heaven does not bless her; she is showy but empty.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jimao of the seventh month of autumn in the twelfth year of Kaiyuan, an edict was issued, saying, "Empress Wang — Heaven does not bless her; she is showy but empty.

sentences.zh: 造起獄訟，朋扇朝廷，見無將之心，有可諱之惡。

translations.literal: She stirs up lawsuits, factions the court, displays a mind for rebellion, and bears evils that cannot be concealed.
translations.idiomatic: She stirs up lawsuits, factions the court, displays a mind for rebellion, and bears evils that cannot be concealed.

sentences.zh: 焉得敬承宗廟，母儀天下？

translations.literal: How can she reverently uphold the ancestral temple and be the mother model for the realm?
translations.idiomatic: How can she reverently uphold the ancestral temple and serve as mother model for the realm?

sentences.zh: 可廢為庶人，別院安置。

translations.literal: She may be deposed as commoner and placed in a separate residence.
translations.idiomatic: She is hereby deposed to commoner status and placed in a separate residence.

sentences.zh: 刑於家室，有愧昔王，為國大計，蓋非獲已。

translations.literal: Punishment within the household shames the kings of old; for the great plan of state, this is surely not done willingly.
translations.idiomatic: To punish her within the household shames the kings of old; for the great plan of state, this is surely not done willingly.

sentences.zh: 」守一賜死。

translations.literal: " Shouyi was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: " Shouyi was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，庶人卒，以一品禮葬於無相寺。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year the commoner died and was buried with first-rank rites at Wuxiang Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year the commoner died and was buried with first-rank rites at Wuxiang Temple.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，雪免，復尊為皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying her name was cleared and she was again honored as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying her name was cleared and she was again honored as empress.

sentences.zh: 貞順皇后武氏

translations.literal: Empress Zhenshun, Lady Wu
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhenshun, Lady Wu

sentences.zh: 玄宗貞順皇后武氏，則天從父兄子恆安王攸止女也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong's Zhenshun Empress, Lady Wu, was the daughter of Prince of Heng'an Youzhi, a son of Wu Zetian's father's elder brother's line.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong's Zhenshun Empress, Lady Wu, was the daughter of Prince of Heng'an Youzhi, a son of Wu Zetian's father's elder brother's line.

sentences.zh: 攸止卒後，后尚幼，隨例入宮。

translations.literal: After Youzhi died, the empress was still young and entered the palace according to custom.
translations.idiomatic: After Youzhi died, she was still young and entered the palace according to custom.

sentences.zh: 上即位，漸承恩寵。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, she gradually received favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ascended the throne, she gradually won his favor.

sentences.zh: 及王庶人廢後，特賜號為惠妃，宮中禮秩，一同皇后。

translations.literal: When the Commoner Wang was deposed as empress, she was specially granted the title Consort Hui; within the palace her ritual rank was the same as the empress's.
translations.idiomatic: When the Commoner Wang was deposed as empress, she was specially granted the title Consort Hui. Within the palace her ritual rank was the same as the empress's.

sentences.zh: 所生母楊氏，封為鄭國夫人。

translations.literal: Her birth mother, Lady Yang, was enfeoffed as Lady of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Her birth mother, Lady Yang, was enfeoffed as Lady of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 同母弟忠，累遷國子祭酒；

translations.literal: Her younger brother by the same mother, Zhong, was cumulatively promoted to Director of the Directorate of Education;
translations.idiomatic: Her younger brother by the same mother, Zhong, was cumulatively promoted to Director of the Directorate of Education;

sentences.zh: 信，秘書監。

translations.literal: Xin became Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xin became Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 惠妃開元初產夏悼王及懷哀王、上仙公主，並繈褓不育，上特垂傷悼。

translations.literal: In the early Kaiyuan era Consort Hui bore Prince Da of Xia, Prince Huai'ai, and Princess Shangxian; all died in infancy, and the emperor was especially grieved.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaiyuan era Consort Hui bore Prince Da of Xia, Prince Huai'ai, and Princess Shangxian. All died in infancy, and the emperor was especially grieved.

sentences.zh: 及生壽王瑁，不敢養於宮中，命寧王憲於外養之。

translations.literal: When she bore Prince of Shou Mao, he did not dare rear him within the palace and ordered Prince of Ning Xian to raise him outside.
translations.idiomatic: When she bore Prince of Shou Mao, he did not dare rear him within the palace and ordered Prince of Ning Xian to raise him outside.

sentences.zh: 又生盛王琦，咸宜、太華二公主。

translations.literal: She also bore Prince of Sheng Qi and the Princesses Xianyi and Taihua.
translations.idiomatic: She also bore Prince of Sheng Qi and the Princesses Xianyi and Taihua.

sentences.zh: 惠妃以開元二十五年十二月薨，年四十餘。

translations.literal: Consort Hui died in the twelfth month of the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan, aged over forty.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Hui died in the twelfth month of the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan, aged over forty.

sentences.zh: 下制曰：「存有懿範，沒有寵章，豈獨被於朝班，故乃施於亞政，可以垂裕，斯為通典。

translations.literal: An edict was issued, saying: "In life there is virtuous example; in death there is favor's seal — not granted to the court ranks alone, but also extended to consorts of secondary rank. What can be handed down as abundance — this is the universal norm.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued, saying, "In life there is virtuous example; in death there is favor's seal — not granted to the court ranks alone, but also extended to consorts of secondary rank. What can be handed down as lasting bounty — this is the universal norm.

sentences.zh: 故惠妃武氏，少而婉順，長而賢明，行合禮經，言應圖史。

translations.literal: Thus Consort Hui, Lady Wu — gentle and compliant in youth, wise and discerning in maturity; conduct accorded with the ritual classics, speech matched the pattern histories.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Consort Hui, Lady Wu — gentle and compliant in youth, wise and discerning in maturity; her conduct accorded with the ritual classics, her speech matched the pattern histories.

sentences.zh: 承戚里之華胄，升後庭之峻秩，貴而不恃，謙而益光。

translations.literal: She inherited the splendid lineage of the imperial consort kin, rose to the exalted rank of the inner court, was noble yet not arrogant, humble yet all the more radiant.
translations.idiomatic: She inherited the splendid lineage of the imperial consort kin and rose to the exalted rank of the inner court. Noble yet not arrogant, humble yet all the more radiant.

sentences.zh: 以道飭躬，以和逮下，四德粲其兼備，六宮咨而是則。

translations.literal: She ordered her person by the Way and reached those below with harmony; the four virtues shone in her combined fullness, and the Six Palaces looked to her as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered her person by the Way and reached those below with harmony. The four virtues shone in her combined fullness, and the Six Palaces looked to her as the standard.

sentences.zh: 法度在己，靡資珩佩；

translations.literal: Law and measure were within herself; she had no need of pendant jades;
translations.idiomatic: Law and measure were within herself; she had no need of pendant jades;

sentences.zh: 躬儉化人，率先絺纮。

translations.literal: Personally frugal, she transformed others, taking the lead in coarse hemp.
translations.idiomatic: Personally frugal, she transformed others, taking the lead in coarse hemp garments.

sentences.zh: 夙有奇表，將加正位，前後固讓，辭而不受，奄至淪歿，載深感悼，遂使玉衣之慶，不及於生前；

translations.literal: Long she had shown a singular mien; the principal rank was about to be added, yet again and again she firmly declined and refused to accept. Suddenly she passed away, and grief was deep; thus the blessing of the jade garment did not reach her in life;
translations.idiomatic: Long she had shown a singular bearing; the principal rank was about to be conferred, yet again and again she firmly declined. Suddenly she passed away, and grief was deep. Thus the blessing of the jade garment did not reach her in life;

sentences.zh: 象服之榮，徒增於身後。

translations.literal: the glory of ceremonial robes with symbolic patterns increased only after her death.
translations.idiomatic: the glory of ceremonial robes with symbolic patterns increased only after her death.

sentences.zh: 可贈貞順皇后，宜令所司擇日冊命。

translations.literal: She may be posthumously granted Empress Zhenshun; the relevant offices should choose a day for investiture.
translations.idiomatic: She is hereby posthumously granted Empress Zhenshun. The relevant offices should choose a day for investiture.

sentences.zh: 」葬於敬陵。

translations.literal: " She was buried at Jing Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: " She was buried at Jing Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 時慶王琮等請制齊衰之服，有司請以忌日廢務，上皆不許之。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Qing Cong and others requested hemp mourning garments be prescribed; the relevant offices requested that business be suspended on the anniversary of her death; the emperor refused all of these.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince of Qing Cong and others requested that hemp mourning garments be prescribed. The relevant offices requested that business be suspended on the anniversary of her death. The emperor refused all of these.

sentences.zh: 立廟於京中昊天觀南，乾元之後，祠享亦絕。

translations.literal: A temple was established south of Haotian Abbey in the capital; after Qianyuan, sacrifices also ceased.
translations.idiomatic: A temple was established south of Haotian Abbey in the capital. After Qianyuan, sacrifices also ceased.

sentences.zh: 楊貴妃

translations.literal: Yang Guifei
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guifei

sentences.zh: 玄宗楊貴妃，高祖令本，金州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong's Yang Guifei — Lingben of Emperor Gaozu's line, Prefect of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Noble Consort Yang of Emperor Xuanzong — her ancestor Lingben had served as Prefect of Jin Prefecture under Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 父玄琰，蜀州司戶。

translations.literal: Her father Xuan Yan was Registrar of Shu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Xuan Yan was Registrar of Shu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 妃早孤，養於叔父河南府士曹玄璬。

translations.literal: The consort was orphaned early and was reared by her uncle Xuan Wei, Assistant in the Henan Prefecture office.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was orphaned early and was reared by her uncle Xuan Wei, Assistant in the Henan Prefecture office.

sentences.zh: 開元初，武惠妃特承寵遇，故王皇后廢黜。

translations.literal: In the early Kaiyuan era, Consort Hui Wu received special favor, and therefore Empress Wang was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaiyuan era, Consort Hui Wu received special favor, and therefore Empress Wang was deposed.

sentences.zh: 二十四年惠妃薨，帝悼惜久之，後庭數千，無可意者。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Consort Hui died; the emperor mourned her long; among the several thousand women of the inner quarters, none pleased him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year Consort Hui died. The emperor mourned her long, and among the several thousand women of the inner quarters, none pleased him.

sentences.zh: 或奏玄琰女姿色冠代，宜蒙召見。

translations.literal: Someone memorialized that Xuan Yan's daughter's beauty surpassed her age and that she ought to be summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Someone memorialized that Xuan Yan's daughter's beauty surpassed her age and that she ought to be summoned for audience.

sentences.zh: 時妃衣道士服，號曰太真。

translations.literal: At that time the consort wore Daoist robes and was styled Taizhen.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the consort wore Daoist robes and was styled Taizhen.

sentences.zh: 既進見，玄宗大悅。

translations.literal: Once she was presented in audience, Emperor Xuanzong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Once she was presented in audience, Emperor Xuanzong was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 不期歲，禮遇如惠妃。

translations.literal: Before a full year had passed, her ceremonial treatment was like that of Consort Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Within less than a year she was honored with ceremony equal to Consort Hui.

sentences.zh: 太真姿質豐艷，善歌舞，通音律，智算過人。

translations.literal: Taizhen's figure and bearing were lush and gorgeous; she was skilled at song and dance, understood musical theory, and her wit and calculation surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhen was voluptuous and radiant in appearance. She danced and sang with skill, mastered musical theory, and her intelligence and shrewdness outstripped those around her.

sentences.zh: 每倩盼承迎，動移上意。

translations.literal: Every time she glanced and welcomed him, she moved the emperor's heart.
translations.idiomatic: With every sidelong glance and show of welcome, she swayed the emperor's mood.

sentences.zh: 宮中呼為「娘子」，禮數實同皇后。

translations.literal: Within the palace she was called "My Lady"; in ritual status she was in truth equal to the empress.
translations.idiomatic: The palace called her "My Lady," and the ceremonials accorded her were effectively those of an empress.

sentences.zh: 有姊三人，皆有才貌，玄宗並封國夫人之號：長曰大姨，封韓國；

translations.literal: She had three elder sisters, all gifted in talent and beauty; Xuanzong jointly enfeoffed them with the title of State Duchess: the eldest, called Elder Aunt, was enfeoffed as Duchess of Han;
translations.idiomatic: She had three elder sisters, all accomplished and beautiful. Xuanzong enfeoffed them all as State Duchesses: the eldest, known as Elder Aunt, received Han;

sentences.zh: 三姨，封虢國；

translations.literal: the third aunt was enfeoffed as Duchess of Guo;
translations.idiomatic: the third, as Duchess of Guo;

sentences.zh: 八姨，封秦國。

translations.literal: the eighth aunt was enfeoffed as Duchess of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: and the eighth, as Duchess of Qin.

sentences.zh: 並承恩澤，出入宮掖，勢傾天下。

translations.literal: All received imperial favor, coming and going within the palace precincts, their power inclining the whole realm.
translations.idiomatic: They all basked in imperial favor, passing in and out of the inner palace until their influence tipped the whole world.

sentences.zh: 妃父玄琰，累贈太尉、齊國公；

translations.literal: The consort's father Xuan Yan was posthumously promoted in succession to Grand Commandant and Duke of Qi;
translations.idiomatic: The consort's father Xuan Yan was posthumously promoted in turn to Grand Commandant and Duke of Qi;

sentences.zh: 母封涼國夫人；

translations.literal: her mother was enfeoffed as Duchess of Liang;
translations.idiomatic: her mother was enfeoffed as Duchess of Liang;

sentences.zh: 叔玄珪，光祿卿。

translations.literal: her uncle Xuan Gui was Director of the Palace Banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Her uncle Xuan Gui served as Director of the Palace Banquets.

sentences.zh: 再從兄銛，鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: Her second cousin Xian was Chamberlain for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: Her second cousin Xian was Chamberlain for Dependencies.

sentences.zh: 锜，侍御史，尚武惠妃女太華公主，以母愛，禮遇過於諸公主，賜甲第，連於宮禁。

translations.literal: Qi was Investigating Censor; he married Princess Taihua, daughter of Martial Consort Hui. Because of his mother's love, his ceremonial treatment exceeded that of the other princesses, and he was granted a premier mansion connected to the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Qi served as Investigating Censor and married Princess Taihua, daughter of Martial Consort Hui. Favored by his mother, he received greater ceremonial honors than the other imperial sons-in-law and was granted a grand residence adjoining the palace grounds.

sentences.zh: 韓、虢、秦三夫人與銛、锜等五家，每有請托，府縣承迎，峻如詔敕，四方賂遺，其門如市。

translations.literal: The three duchesses of Han, Guo, and Qin together with Xian, Qi, and the other five families—whenever they made requests, prefectures and counties received them with the severity of an imperial edict; bribes from all quarters came until their gates were like a marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: The three duchesses of Han, Guo, and Qin, together with Xian, Qi, and the other five Yang households, had only to ask and prefectures and counties obeyed as sternly as if an edict had come down. Gifts poured in from every direction until their gates thronged like a market.

sentences.zh: 皇場五載七月，貴妃以微譴送歸楊銛宅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Huangchang, seventh month, the Noble Consort was sent back to Yang Xian's residence on account of a slight offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year of the Tianbao era, the Noble Consort was sent back to Yang Xian's residence over a minor rebuke.

sentences.zh: 比至亭午，上思之，不食。

translations.literal: By the time noon arrived, the emperor was thinking of her and would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: By midday he was already missing her and refused to eat.

sentences.zh: 高力士探知上旨，請送貴妃院供帳、器玩、廩餼等辦具百餘車，上又分御饌以送之。

translations.literal: Gao Lishi probed the emperor's intent and requested that more than a hundred cartloads of furnishings for the Noble Consort's quarters—bedding, vessels and curios, and provisions—be sent; the emperor also sent portions of the imperial table.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi discerned the emperor's mood and asked that more than a hundred cartloads of bedding, furnishings, playthings, and provisions be sent to the Noble Consort's residence. The emperor also sent dishes from his own table.

sentences.zh: 帝動不稱旨，暴怒笞撻左右。

translations.literal: The emperor, displeased at every turn, flew into rage and beat the attendants at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing around him pleased him; he flew into rages and had his attendants beaten.

sentences.zh: 力士伏奏請迎貴妃歸院。

translations.literal: Lishi prostrated himself and memorialized, requesting that the Noble Consort be welcomed back to her quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi prostrated himself and asked that the Noble Consort be brought back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 是夜，開安興里門入內，妃伏地謝罪，上歡然慰撫。

translations.literal: That night he opened the gate at Anxing Ward and she entered the inner palace; the consort prostrated herself to confess guilt, and the emperor gladly comforted her.
translations.idiomatic: That night the gate of Anxing Ward was opened and she was admitted to the inner palace. She prostrated herself in apology, and the emperor received her back with evident joy.

sentences.zh: 翌日，韓、虢進食，上作樂終日，左右暴有賜與。

translations.literal: The next day the duchesses of Han and Guo brought food; the emperor made music all day, and those at his side suddenly received lavish gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the duchesses of Han and Guo sent food. Music played all day, and those around the emperor received sudden, lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 自是寵遇愈隆。

translations.literal: From then on favor grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: From then on her favor only grew.

sentences.zh: 韓、虢、秦三夫人歲給錢千貫，為脂粉之資。

translations.literal: The three duchesses of Han, Guo, and Qin were allotted a thousand strings of cash each year as funds for cosmetics.
translations.idiomatic: The three duchesses of Han, Guo, and Qin each received a thousand strings of cash every year for rouge and powder.

sentences.zh: 銛授三品、上柱國，私第立戟。

translations.literal: Xian was appointed Third Rank and Upper Pillar of the State, and halberds were erected at his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was made a third-rank official and Upper Pillar of the State, and ceremonial halberds were set up at his private residence.

sentences.zh: 姊妹昆仲五家，甲第洞開，僭擬宮掖，車馬僕禦，照耀京邑，遞相誇尚。

translations.literal: The five families of sisters and brothers—all their mansions stood open in splendor, rivaling the palace precincts; chariots, horses, and servants blazed across the capital, each outdoing the other in display.
translations.idiomatic: The five Yang households of sisters and brothers kept their grand mansions thrown wide, aping the inner palace. Chariots, horses, and retinues lit up the capital as they vied to outshine one another.

sentences.zh: 每構一堂，費逾千萬計，見制度宏壯於己者，即撤而復造，土木之工，不舍晝夜。

translations.literal: Every time they built a hall, the cost exceeded ten million; when they saw another's structure more grand than their own, they demolished it and rebuilt—carpentry and masonry never ceased day or night.
translations.idiomatic: Each new hall cost more than ten million cash. If they saw another house grander than theirs, they tore theirs down and built again. Construction went on without pause, day and night.

sentences.zh: 玄宗頒賜及四方獻遺，五家如一，中使不絕。

translations.literal: Whatever Xuanzong bestowed and whatever tribute came from the four quarters, the five families received alike; palace envoys never stopped coming.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever Xuanzong granted and whatever gifts arrived from the four quarters, the five households shared equally, and palace envoys were constantly on the road.

sentences.zh: 開元已來，豪貴雄盛，無如楊氏之比也。

translations.literal: Since the Kaiyuan era, no noble house had been so mighty and splendid as the Yang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Kaiyuan era, no clan had been so powerful and splendid as the Yang.

sentences.zh: 玄宗凡有遊幸，貴妃無不隨侍，乘馬則高力士執轡授鞭。

translations.literal: Whenever Xuanzong went on excursions, the Noble Consort always attended; when she rode horseback, Gao Lishi held the reins and presented the whip.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xuanzong traveled, the Noble Consort always accompanied him. When she rode, Gao Lishi held the reins and handed her the whip.

sentences.zh: 宮中供貴妃院織錦刺繡之工，凡七百人，其雕刻熔造，又數百人。

translations.literal: Within the palace, those who supplied the Noble Consort's quarters with brocade weaving and embroidery numbered seven hundred in all; those for carving, casting, and manufacture numbered several hundred more.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace, seven hundred artisans wove brocade and embroidery for the Noble Consort's residence, and several hundred more worked in carving, casting, and metalwork.

sentences.zh: 揚、益、嶺表刺史，必求良工造作奇器異服，以奉貴妃獻賀，因致擢居顯位。

translations.literal: Prefects of Yang, Yi, and the Lingnan region invariably sought skilled craftsmen to make exotic vessels and strange garments, offering them to the Noble Consort as congratulatory gifts—and thereby rose to eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects of Yangzhou, Yizhou, and the Lingnan region invariably sought master craftsmen to produce rare vessels and extraordinary garments, presenting them to the Noble Consort as tribute—and in this way won promotion to high office.

sentences.zh: 玄宗每年十月幸華清宮，國忠姊妹五家扈從，每家為一隊，著一色衣，五家合隊，照映如百花之煥發，而遺鈿墜舄，瑟瑟珠翠，燦爛芳馥於路。

translations.literal: Each year in the tenth month Xuanzong visited Huaqing Palace; Guozhong and the five families of his sisters followed in attendance. Each family formed its own column, dressed in a single color; when the five columns merged, they shone like a hundred flowers bursting into bloom, and along the road lost hairpins, fallen shoes, tinkling gems, and pearl and jade glittered in radiant fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: Each tenth month Xuanzong visited Huaqing Palace, and Guozhong with the five Yang households followed in attendance. Each family marched in its own column dressed in one color; when the five columns merged, they blazed like a hundred flowers in bloom. Lost hairpins, fallen shoes, tinkling ornaments, pearls, and jade littered the road in glittering, perfumed profusion.

sentences.zh: 而國忠私於虢國而不避雄狐之刺，每入朝或聯鑣方駕，不施帷幔。

translations.literal: Yet Guozhong carried on privately with the Duchess of Guo without heeding the sting of "the male fox"; whenever he entered court or they rode side by side in matched carriages, they drew no curtain.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong carried on a private affair with the Duchess of Guo without caring who might gossip, and when he went to court or they rode side by side in matched carriages, they did not even draw a curtain.

sentences.zh: 每三朝慶賀，五鼓待漏，艷妝盈巷，蠟炬如晝。

translations.literal: At each of the thrice-monthly court celebrations, before the fifth watch they waited for the dawn signal; painted faces filled the lanes, wax torches bright as noonday.
translations.idiomatic: At each thrice-monthly court celebration they waited before the fifth watch for the water-clock signal. Painted faces filled the lanes, and wax torches burned bright as noon.

sentences.zh: 而十宅諸王百孫院婚嫁，皆因韓、虢為紹介，仍先納賂千貫而奏請，罔不稱旨。

translations.literal: For marriages within the Ten Residence princes and the Court of Hundred Grandsons, Han and Guo invariably served as go-betweens; one still paid a bribe of a thousand strings first and then memorialized—and none failed to meet the emperor's wish.
translations.idiomatic: Marriages among the princes of the Ten Residences and the Court of Hundred Grandsons all went through Han and Guo as matchmakers. A bribe of a thousand strings was paid first, then the memorial was submitted—and every request won the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 天寶九載，貴妃復忤旨，送歸外第。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianbao, the Noble Consort again offended the emperor's intent and was sent back to her outside residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Tianbao the Noble Consort again gave offense and was sent back to her residence outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 時吉溫與中貴人善，溫入奏曰：「婦人智識不遠，有忤聖情，然貴妃久承恩顧，何惜宮中一席之地，使其就戮，安忍取辱於外哉！

translations.literal: At that time Ji Wen was on good terms with a palace eunuch of influence. Wen entered and memorialized: "A woman's knowledge and judgment do not extend far; she may have offended the sacred mood. Yet the Noble Consort has long received your gracious favor—why begrudge her a single place within the palace? To let her face execution would be unbearable; how could you endure that she suffer disgrace outside?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ji Wen was close to an influential palace eunuch. Wen entered and said, "A woman's wit does not reach far, and she may have offended Your Majesty. Yet the Noble Consort has long enjoyed your favor. Why begrudge her a place in the palace? To leave her to die would be cruel enough; how can you bear to let her be shamed outside?"

sentences.zh: 」上即令中使張韜光賜御饌，妃附韜光泣奏曰：「妾忤聖顏，罪當萬死。

translations.literal: " The emperor immediately ordered the palace envoy Zhang Taoguang to convey imperial viands. The consort, through Taoguang, tearfully memorialized: "Your servant offended the sacred countenance and deserves ten thousand deaths."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor at once sent the palace envoy Zhang Taoguang with food from the imperial table. Through Taoguang the consort tearfully said, "Your servant has offended Your Majesty and deserves death ten thousand times over."

sentences.zh: 衣服之外，皆聖恩所賜，無可遺留，然髮膚是父母所有。

translations.literal: Apart from clothing, all is bestowed by your sacred grace; nothing can be returned. Yet hair and skin belong to one's parents."
translations.idiomatic: Apart from my clothes, everything I have is your gift and cannot be returned. But hair and skin are what my parents gave me."

sentences.zh: 」乃引刀翦髮一繚附獻。

translations.literal: " She then took a knife, cut off a lock of hair, and sent it as an offering.
translations.idiomatic: " She then took a knife, cut off a lock of hair, and sent it with her message.

sentences.zh: 玄宗見之驚惋，即使力士召還。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong saw it he was shocked and grieved, and immediately sent Lishi to summon her back.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong saw it he was shaken and grieved, and at once sent Lishi to bring her back.

sentences.zh: 國忠既居宰執，兼領劍南節度，勢漸恣橫。

translations.literal: Once Guozhong had risen to chief minister and also held the Jiannan governorship, his power grew increasingly overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guozhong became chief minister and also held the Jiannan governorship, his power grew ever more arrogant and overbearing.

sentences.zh: 十載正月望夜，楊家五宅夜遊，與廣平公主騎從爭西市門。

translations.literal: On the lantern night of the first month of the tenth year, the five Yang residences went out at night and quarreled with the mounted retinue of the Princess of Guangping at the gate of the West Market.
translations.idiomatic: On the lantern festival night of the first month of the tenth year, the five Yang households went out after dark and clashed with the mounted escort of the Princess of Guangping at the West Market gate.

sentences.zh: 楊氏奴揮鞭及公主衣，公主墮馬，駙馬程昌裔扶主，因及數撾。

translations.literal: A Yang clansman's slave whipped and struck the princess's garment; the princess fell from her horse. Her consort Cheng Changyi helped his mistress and in the process took several blows himself.
translations.idiomatic: A Yang household slave struck the princess's clothing with his whip, and she fell from her horse. Her consort Cheng Changyi helped her up and himself took several blows.

sentences.zh: 公主泣奏之，上令殺楊氏奴，昌裔亦停官。

translations.literal: The princess wept and reported it; the emperor ordered the Yang clansman's slave killed, and Changyi was also suspended from office.
translations.idiomatic: The princess wept and reported the affair. The emperor ordered the Yang slave executed, and Changyi was also removed from office.

sentences.zh: 國忠二男昢、暄，妃弟鑒，皆尚公主，楊氏一門尚二公主、二郡主。

translations.literal: Guozhong's two sons Pan and Xuan, and the consort's younger brother Jian, all married princesses; the Yang clan as a whole had married two princesses and two commandery princesses.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong's two sons Pan and Xuan, together with the consort's younger brother Jian, all married princesses. The Yang clan as a whole had taken two princesses and two commandery princesses in marriage.

sentences.zh: 貴妃父祖立私廟，玄宗御制家廟碑文並書。

translations.literal: The Noble Consort's forebears established a private temple; Xuanzong personally composed the text of the family temple stele and wrote it in his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: The Noble Consort's ancestors were given a private temple, and Xuanzong personally composed and wrote the text of the family shrine stele.

sentences.zh: 玄珪累遷至兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Xuan Gui was promoted in succession to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Gui rose in succession to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，范陽節度使安祿山大立邊功，上深寵之。

translations.literal: During the Tianbao era, An Lushu, military governor of Fanyang, achieved great merit on the frontier, and the emperor deeply favored him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era An Lushan, military governor of Fanyang, won great victories on the frontier, and the emperor favored him deeply.

sentences.zh: 祿山來朝，帝令貴妃姊妹與祿山結為兄弟。

translations.literal: When Lushan came to court, the emperor had the Noble Consort's sisters enter brotherhood with Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan came to court, the emperor had the Noble Consort's sisters swear brotherhood with him.

sentences.zh: 祿山母事貴妃，每宴賜，錫賚稠沓。

translations.literal: Lushan treated the Noble Consort as his mother; at every banquet the gifts conferred were thick and frequent.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan treated the Noble Consort as his adoptive mother, and at every feast the rewards he received were lavish and unceasing.

sentences.zh: 及祿山叛，露檄數國忠之罪。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, he issued a public proclamation enumerating Guozhong's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled, he published an open proclamation listing Guozhong's crimes.

sentences.zh: 河北盜起，玄宗以皇太子為天下兵馬元帥，監撫軍國事。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Hebei; Xuanzong appointed the Crown Prince supreme commander of all armed forces under Heaven to oversee and govern military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Hebei, Xuanzong made the Crown Prince supreme commander of all armies under Heaven to oversee military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 國忠大懼，諸楊聚哭，貴妃銜土陳請，帝遂不行內禪。

translations.literal: Guozhong was greatly afraid; the Yang clansmen gathered and wept; the Noble Consort held earth in her mouth and petitioned repeatedly, and the emperor then did not proceed with abdication within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong was terrified. The Yang clan gathered and wept, and the Noble Consort petitioned with earth held in her mouth as a sign of abject humility. The emperor then abandoned the planned inner abdication.

sentences.zh: 及潼關失守，從幸至馬嵬，禁軍大將陳玄禮密啟太子，誅國忠父子。

translations.literal: When Tong Pass fell, as he followed the emperor in flight to Mawei, the chief general of the imperial guard Chen Xuanli secretly reported to the Crown Prince to execute Guozhong and his sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Pass fell and the court fled as far as Mawei, Chen Xuanli, chief general of the imperial guard, secretly urged the Crown Prince to execute Guozhong and his sons.

sentences.zh: 既而四軍不散，玄宗遣力士宣問，對曰「賊本尚在」，蓋指貴妃也。

translations.literal: Then the four armies did not disperse; Xuanzong sent Lishi to announce inquiry, and they replied, "The root of the rebels is still present"—meaning the Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: The four armies still would not disband. Xuanzong sent Lishi to ask why, and they answered, "The root of the rebellion is still here"—meaning the Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 力士復奏，帝不獲已，與妃詔，遂縊死於佛室。

translations.literal: Lishi memorialized again; the emperor, unable to do otherwise, spoke with the consort under edict, and she was then strangled to death in the Buddha hall.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi reported again. Unable to refuse, the emperor spoke with the consort by edict, and she was strangled in the Buddha hall.

sentences.zh: 時年三十八，瘞於驛西道側。

translations.literal: She was then thirty-eight years old, and was buried beside the post road west of the station.
translations.idiomatic: She was thirty-eight. She was buried beside the post road west of the station.

sentences.zh: 上皇自蜀還，令中使祭奠，詔令改葬。

translations.literal: After the Retired Emperor returned from Shu, he ordered palace envoys to offer sacrifices and issued an edict for reburial.
translations.idiomatic: After the Retired Emperor returned from Shu, he sent palace envoys to offer sacrifices and ordered that she be reburied.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎李揆曰：「龍武將士誅國忠，以其負國兆亂。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Li Kui said: "The Dragon Martial guardsmen executed Guozhong because he betrayed the state and presaged rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Li Kui said, "The Dragon Martial guards executed Guozhong because he betrayed the state and brought on rebellion.

sentences.zh: 今改葬故妃，恐將士疑懼，葬禮未可行。

translations.literal: Now to rebury the former consort would make the guardsmen suspicious and afraid; the burial rites cannot yet be carried out."
translations.idiomatic: If the former consort is now reburied with honor, the troops may grow suspicious and afraid. The funeral cannot be carried out yet."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " It was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 上皇密令中使改葬於他所。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor secretly ordered palace envoys to rebury her elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor secretly ordered palace envoys to move her burial to another place.

sentences.zh: 初瘞時以紫褥裹之，肌膚已壞，而香囊仍在。

translations.literal: At the first burial she had been wrapped in a purple quilt; the flesh had already decayed, but the perfumed pouch remained.
translations.idiomatic: At the first burial she had been wrapped in a purple quilt. The flesh had already decayed, but her perfumed pouch remained intact.

sentences.zh: 內官以獻，上皇視之淒惋，乃令圖其形於別殿，朝夕視之。

translations.literal: Inner attendants presented it; when the Retired Emperor saw it he was grief-stricken, and ordered her likeness painted in a separate hall, viewing it morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants brought it to him. The Retired Emperor looked on it with bitter grief and ordered her likeness painted in a separate hall, which he gazed at morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 馬嵬之誅國忠也，虢國夫人聞難作，奔馬至陳倉。

translations.literal: At the execution of Guozhong at Mawei, the Duchess of Guo heard calamity had broken out and galloped to Chencang.
translations.idiomatic: When Guozhong was killed at Mawei, the Duchess of Guo heard trouble had broken out and galloped to Chencang.

sentences.zh: 縣令薛景仙率人吏追之，走入竹林。

translations.literal: Magistrate Xue Jingxian led clerks and men in pursuit; she ran into a bamboo grove.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Xue Jingxian led clerks and men in pursuit until she fled into a bamboo grove.

sentences.zh: 先殺其男裴徽及一女。

translations.literal: First they killed her son Pei Hui and one daughter.
translations.idiomatic: They first killed her son Pei Hui and one daughter.

sentences.zh: 國忠妻裴柔曰：「娘子為我盡命。

translations.literal: Guozhong's wife Pei Rou said: "My Lady, grant me death."
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong's wife Pei Rou said, "My Lady, do me the mercy of ending my life."

sentences.zh: 」即刺殺之。

translations.literal: " She then stabbed and killed her.
translations.idiomatic: " She then stabbed her to death.

sentences.zh: 已而自刎，不死，縣吏載之，閉於獄中。

translations.literal: Afterwards she cut her own throat but did not die; the county officers loaded her into a cart and shut her in prison.
translations.idiomatic: She then cut her own throat but did not die. The county officers loaded her into a cart and shut her in jail.

sentences.zh: 猶謂吏曰：「國家乎？

translations.literal: She still said to the officers: "The state?
translations.idiomatic: She still asked the officers, "Are you men of the state?

sentences.zh: 賊乎？

translations.literal: Or rebels?"
translations.idiomatic: Or rebels?"

sentences.zh: 」吏曰：「互有之。

translations.literal: " The officers said: "Both, in part."
translations.idiomatic: " They answered, "A little of both."

sentences.zh: 」血凝至喉而卒，遂瘞於郭外。

translations.literal: " Blood congealed to her throat and she died; she was then buried outside the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: " Blood clotted in her throat and she died. She was buried outside the city wall.

sentences.zh: 韓國夫人婿秘書少監崔峋，女為代宗妃。

translations.literal: The son-in-law of the Duchess of Han, Vice Director of the Secretariat Cui Xun—his daughter became a consort of Emperor Daizong.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xun, Vice Director of the Secretariat and son-in-law of the Duchess of Han, had a daughter who became a consort of Emperor Daizong.

sentences.zh: 虢國男裴徽尚代宗女延安公主，女嫁讓帝男。

translations.literal: The Duchess of Guo's son Pei Hui married Emperor Daizong's daughter, the Princess of Yan'an; her daughter married a son of the Prince of Yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Hui, son of the Duchess of Guo, married Emperor Daizong's daughter, the Princess of Yan'an; his daughter married a son of the Prince of Yielding.

sentences.zh: 秦國夫人婿柳澄先死，男鈞尚長清縣主，澄弟潭尚肅宗女和政公主。

translations.literal: The son-in-law of the Duchess of Qin, Liu Cheng, had died first; his son Jun married the Princess of Changqing, a commandery princess; Cheng's younger brother Tan married Emperor Suzong's daughter, the Princess of Hezheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cheng, son-in-law of the Duchess of Qin, had already died. His son Jun married the Princess of Changqing, a commandery princess, and Cheng's younger brother Tan married Emperor Suzong's daughter, the Princess of Hezheng.
